Natural_Language: This part prescribes requirements for obtaining financial protection against losses under contracts that result from the use of the sealed bid or negotiated methods. It covers bid guarantees, bonds, alternative payment protections, security for bonds, and insurance.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_000_a: Part 28 prescribes requirements for obtaining financial protection against losses under contracts using sealed bid or negotiated methods; P_28_000_b: Part 28 covers bid guarantees; P_28_000_c: Part 28 covers bonds; P_28_000_d: Part 28 covers alternative payment protections; P_28_000_e: Part 28 covers security for bonds; P_28_000_f: Part 28 covers insurance
Validation_Notes: Scope statement. Six conjunctive elements describing Part 28 coverage areas. Straightforward conjunction of declarative statements.

Natural_Language: Definitions. As used in this part, the following terms are defined (parent aggregating 8 defined terms: attorney-in-fact, bid, bid guarantee, bidder, bond, consent of surety, penal sum, reinsurance).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_001: Part 28 definitions section establishing meanings for 8 terms
Formal_Logic_Statement: P_28_001_def_atty ^ P_28_001_def_bid ^ P_28_001_def_bidguar ^ P_28_001_def_bidder ^ P_28_001_def_bond ^ P_28_001_def_consent ^ P_28_001_def_penal ^ P_28_001_def_reins
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition aggregating all definitions. All terms defined conjunctively within Part 28 scope.

Natural_Language: Attorney-in-fact means an agent, independent agent, underwriter, or any other company or individual holding a power of attorney granted by a surety.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_001_def_atty_a: Entity is an agent; P_28_001_def_atty_b: Entity is an independent agent; P_28_001_def_atty_c: Entity is an underwriter; P_28_001_def_atty_d: Entity is any other company or individual holding a power of attorney granted by a surety
Formal_Logic_Statement: (P_28_001_def_atty_a v P_28_001_def_atty_b v P_28_001_def_atty_c v P_28_001_def_atty_d) -> Attorney_in_Fact
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive definition: any of four categories qualifies. Rule 15 used for definitional implication. The disjunction is inclusive; multiple categories could apply simultaneously.

Natural_Language: Bid means any response to a solicitation, including a proposal under a negotiated acquisition.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_001_def_bid_a: Entity is a response to a solicitation; P_28_001_def_bid_b: Definition includes proposals under negotiated acquisitions
Validation_Notes: Broad definitional statement. The 'including' clause is additive clarification, not a separate condition. Conjunction appropriate because the definition encompasses both elements.

Natural_Language: Bid guarantee means a form of security assuring that the bidder (1) will not withdraw a bid within the period specified for acceptance; and (2) will execute a written contract and furnish required bonds within the time specified. (Parent aggregating (1) and (2).)
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_001_def_bidguar: Bid guarantee is a form of security assuring bidder compliance with sub-requirements (1) and (2)
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. The 'and' connector between (1) and (2) makes this conjunctive. Both assurances are required for the definition to be satisfied.

Natural_Language: Will not withdraw a bid within the period specified for acceptance.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_001_def_bidguar_1: Bidder will not withdraw bid within the acceptance period
Validation_Notes: Simple negation. The bid guarantee assures that the bidder will NOT withdraw. Atomic proposition.

Natural_Language: Will execute a written contract and furnish required bonds, including any necessary coinsurance or reinsurance agreements, within the time specified in the bid, unless a longer time allowed, after receipt of the specified forms.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_001_def_bidguar_2_a: Bidder will execute a written contract within specified time; P_28_001_def_bidguar_2_b: Bidder will furnish required bonds including coinsurance/reinsurance within specified time; P_28_001_def_bidguar_2_c: Longer time may be allowed
Validation_Notes: Execute contract AND furnish bonds are conjunctive requirements. The 'unless a longer time allowed' creates a disjunctive alternative to the time constraint rather than negating the obligation itself. Marked PENDING_REVIEW due to ambiguity in how the time extension interacts with the base obligations.

Natural_Language: Bidder means any entity that is responding or has responded to a solicitation, including an offeror under a negotiated acquisition.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_001_def_bidder_a: Entity is currently responding to a solicitation; P_28_001_def_bidder_b: Entity has responded to a solicitation; P_28_001_def_bidder_c: Definition includes offerors under negotiated acquisitions
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive temporal scope (is responding OR has responded) combined conjunctively with the clarifying inclusion of negotiated acquisition offerors.

Natural_Language: Bond means a written instrument executed by a bidder or contractor (the 'principal'), and a second party (the 'surety' or 'sureties') (except as provided in 28.204), to assure fulfillment of the principal's obligations to a third party (the 'obligee' or 'Government'), identified in the bond. If the principal's obligations are not met, the bond assures payment, to the extent stipulated, of any loss sustained by the obligee. The types of bonds and related documents are as follows: (parent aggregating (1)-(6)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_001_def_bond_a: Bond is a written instrument executed by principal and surety (except 28.204); P_28_001_def_bond_b: Bond assures fulfillment of principal obligations to obligee; P_28_001_def_bond_c: If obligations not met then bond assures payment of loss; P_28_001_def_bond_d: Six types of bonds defined in (1)-(6)
Formal_Logic_Statement: P_28_001_def_bond_a ^ P_28_001_def_bond_b ^ (~Obligations_Met -> Payment_of_Loss) ^ (P_28_001_def_bond_1 v P_28_001_def_bond_2 v P_28_001_def_bond_3 v P_28_001_def_bond_4 v P_28_001_def_bond_5 v P_28_001_def_bond_6)
Justification_Rules: Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Complex parent definition. Core definition is conjunctive. The remedial clause ('If obligations not met') is a conditional triggering payment assurance. The six bond types are disjunctive categories. Exception for 28.204 noted as dependency. Rule 15 used for the conditional payment trigger.

Natural_Language: An advance payment bond secures fulfillment of the contractor's obligations under an advance payment provision.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_001_def_bond_1: Advance payment bond secures contractor obligations under advance payment provision
Validation_Notes: Definitional implication: the bond type implies its security function. Rule 15 appropriate for definitional linkage. Straightforward but flagged per HIGH-RISK protocol.

Natural_Language: An annual bid bond is a single bond furnished by a bidder, in lieu of separate bid bonds, which secures all bids (on other than construction contracts) requiring bonds submitted during a specific Government fiscal year.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_001_def_bond_2_a: Annual bid bond is a single bond in lieu of separate bid bonds; P_28_001_def_bond_2_b: Covers bids on other than construction contracts; P_28_001_def_bond_2_c: Covers bids requiring bonds submitted during a specific Government fiscal year
Validation_Notes: Three conjunctive defining characteristics. All three elements must be present for the definition to apply. Exclusion of construction contracts is an embedded restriction.

Natural_Language: An annual performance bond is a single bond furnished by a contractor, in lieu of separate performance bonds, to secure fulfillment of the contractor's obligations under contracts (other than construction contracts) requiring bonds entered into during a specific Government fiscal year.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_001_def_bond_3_a: Annual performance bond is a single bond in lieu of separate performance bonds; P_28_001_def_bond_3_b: Covers contracts other than construction; P_28_001_def_bond_3_c: Covers contracts requiring bonds entered into during a specific Government fiscal year
Validation_Notes: Parallel structure to annual bid bond definition. Three conjunctive elements. Construction exclusion embedded.

Natural_Language: A patent infringement bond secures fulfillment of the contractor's obligations under a patent provision.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_001_def_bond_4: Patent infringement bond secures contractor obligations under patent provision
Validation_Notes: Definitional implication linking bond type to its function. Rule 15 flagged per protocol.

Natural_Language: A payment bond assures payments as required by law to all persons supplying labor or material in the prosecution of the work provided for in the contract.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_001_def_bond_5_a: Payment bond assures payments required by law; P_28_001_def_bond_5_b: Payments go to all persons supplying labor or material for the contract work
Validation_Notes: Two conjunctive elements: legal requirement for payment AND scope of covered persons. Both must hold.

Natural_Language: A performance bond secures performance and fulfillment of the contractor's obligations under the contract.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_001_def_bond_6: Performance bond secures performance and fulfillment of contractor contract obligations
Validation_Notes: Definitional implication with conjunctive consequent. Bond type implies both performance security and fulfillment security. Rule 15 flagged.

Natural_Language: Consent of surety means an acknowledgment by a surety that its bond given in connection with a contract continues to apply to the contract as modified.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_001_def_consent_a: Consent is an acknowledgment by surety; P_28_001_def_consent_b: Bond continues to apply to contract as modified
Validation_Notes: Two conjunctive definitional elements: the nature of consent (acknowledgment) and its effect (continued applicability to modified contract).

Natural_Language: Penal sum or penal amount means the amount of money specified in a bond (or a percentage of the bid price in a bid bond) as the maximum payment for which the surety is obligated or the amount of security required to be pledged to the Government in lieu of a corporate or individual surety for the bond.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_001_def_penal_a: Penal sum is the amount specified in a bond as maximum surety obligation; P_28_001_def_penal_b: In a bid bond it may be expressed as a percentage of bid price; P_28_001_def_penal_c: Alternatively it is the amount of security pledged in lieu of surety
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive definition: penal sum can be expressed as a fixed amount, a percentage (for bid bonds), or the pledged security amount. The 'or' connectors make this a three-way disjunction.

Natural_Language: Reinsurance means a transaction which provides that a surety, for a consideration, agrees to indemnify another surety against loss which the latter may sustain under a bond which it has issued.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_001_def_reins_a: Reinsurance is a transaction; P_28_001_def_reins_b: One surety agrees to indemnify another surety for consideration; P_28_001_def_reins_c: Indemnification is against loss under a bond issued by the indemnified surety
Validation_Notes: Three conjunctive definitional elements. All must hold for the term to apply. Straightforward definition with no conditional triggers.

Natural_Language: This subpart prescribes requirements and procedures for the use of bonds, alternative payment protections, and all types of bid guarantees.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_100_a: Subpart 28.1 prescribes requirements and procedures for bonds; P_28_100_b: Subpart 28.1 prescribes requirements for alternative payment protections; P_28_100_c: Subpart 28.1 prescribes requirements for all types of bid guarantees
Validation_Notes: Scope statement for Subpart 28.1. Three conjunctive coverage areas.

Natural_Language: Bid guarantees (parent aggregating 28.101-1 through 28.101-4).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_101: Bid guarantee requirements as specified in subsections 28.101-1 through 28.101-4
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition aggregating four subsections covering policy, solicitation provisions, attorney-in-fact authority, and noncompliance.

Natural_Language: Policy on use (parent aggregating (a)-(c)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_101_1: Bid guarantee policy requirements as specified in paragraphs (a) through (c)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating three policy paragraphs on bid guarantee usage.

Natural_Language: A contracting officer must not require a bid guarantee unless a performance bond or a performance and payment bond is also required (see 28.102 and 28.103). Except as provided in paragraph (c) of this subsection, bid guarantees must be required whenever a performance bond or a performance and payment bond is required.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_101_1_a_1: CO must not require bid guarantee unless performance bond or performance and payment bond also required; P_28_101_1_a_2: Except as provided in (c) bid guarantees must be required whenever performance bond or performance and payment bond is required
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Modus Tollens (MT): Rule 2; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7
Validation_Notes: Two-part rule. First: negative conditional prohibiting bid guarantee without performance bond. Second: affirmative mandate requiring bid guarantee when performance bond required, subject to (c) waiver exception. Rule 15 used for both conditionals. Cross-references 28.102 and 28.103.

Natural_Language: All types of bid guarantees are acceptable for supply or service contracts (see annual bid bonds and annual performance bonds coverage in 28.001). Only separate bid guarantees are acceptable in connection with construction contracts. Agencies may specify that only separate bid bonds are acceptable in connection with construction contracts.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_101_1_b_1: All types of bid guarantees acceptable for supply/service contracts; P_28_101_1_b_2: Only separate bid guarantees acceptable for construction contracts; P_28_101_1_b_3: Agencies may specify only separate bid bonds for construction
Justification_Rules: Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Conjunctive policy with embedded permissive 'may' for agency specification authority. The restriction to separate bid guarantees for construction is mandatory; agency further specification is discretionary. Rule 15/18 for the permissive clause.

Natural_Language: The chief of the contracting office may waive the requirement to obtain a bid guarantee when a performance bond or a performance and payment bond is required if it is determined that a bid guarantee is not in the best interest of the Government for a specific acquisition (e.g., overseas construction, emergency acquisitions, sole-source contracts). Class waivers may be authorized by the agency head or designee.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_101_1_c_1: Chief of contracting office may waive bid guarantee requirement when performance bond required and not in Government best interest; P_28_101_1_c_2: Class waivers may be authorized by agency head or designee
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7
Validation_Notes: Two permissive authorities. Both use 'may' indicating discretion not mandate. First: individual waiver by chief of contracting office under specific conditions. Second: class waiver authority at agency head level. Tautology in consequent reflects discretionary nature.

Natural_Language: Solicitation provision or contract clause (parent aggregating (a)-(b)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_101_2: Solicitation provision/clause requirements as specified in (a) and (b)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating provision insertion requirement and amount determination.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer must insert a provision or clause substantially the same as the provision at 52.228-1, Bid Guarantee, in solicitations or contracts that require a bid guarantee or similar guarantee. For example, the contracting officer may modify this provision- (parent with (1)-(4)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_101_2_a_1: CO must insert provision substantially same as 52.228-1 when bid guarantee required; P_28_101_2_a_2: CO may modify the provision per (1)-(4)
Validation_Notes: Mandatory insertion triggered by bid guarantee requirement. Modification authority is permissive. The four sub-paragraphs describe optional modifications. Cross-references 52.228-1.

Natural_Language: To set a period of time that is other than 10 days for the return of executed bonds.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_101_2_a_1: CO may modify 52.228-1 to set a return period other than 10 days for executed bonds
Validation_Notes: Optional modification scenario. Permissive authority inherited from parent (a). Specifies the default 10-day period can be altered.

Natural_Language: For use in connection with construction solicitations when the agency has specified that only separate bid bonds are acceptable in accordance with 28.101-1(b).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_101_2_a_2: CO may modify 52.228-1 for construction solicitations when agency specifies only separate bid bonds per 28.101-1(b)
Validation_Notes: Conditional modification: both construction context AND agency specification must be present. Cross-references 28.101-1(b).

Natural_Language: For use in solicitations for negotiated contracts.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_101_2_a_3: CO may modify 52.228-1 for use in solicitations for negotiated contracts
Validation_Notes: Permissive modification scenario for negotiated contracts. Discretionary per parent (a).

Natural_Language: For use in service contracts containing options for extended performance.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_101_2_a_4: CO may modify 52.228-1 for service contracts with extended performance options
Validation_Notes: Permissive modification scenario for service contracts with options. Discretionary per parent (a).

Natural_Language: The contracting officer must determine the amount of the bid guarantee for insertion in the provision at 52.228-1 (see 28.102-2(a)). The amount must be adequate to protect the Government from loss should the successful bidder fail to execute further contractual documents and bonds as required. The bid guarantee amount must be at least 20 percent of the bid price but must not exceed $3 million. When the penal sum is expressed as a percentage, a maximum dollar limitation may be stated.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_101_2_b_1: CO must determine bid guarantee amount for 52.228-1; P_28_101_2_b_2: Amount must be adequate to protect Government from loss if bidder fails to execute; P_28_101_2_b_3: Amount must be at least 20% of bid price; P_28_101_2_b_4: Amount must not exceed $3 million; P_28_101_2_b_5: When penal sum expressed as percentage a maximum dollar limitation may be stated
Justification_Rules: Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Four mandatory conjunctive requirements plus one permissive conditional. The 20% floor and $3M ceiling create a bounded range. The percentage/dollar limitation clause is permissive. Cross-references 28.102-2(a) and 52.228-1.

Natural_Language: Authority of an attorney-in-fact for a bid bond (parent aggregating (a)-(f)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_101_3: Attorney-in-fact authority requirements as specified in (a) through (f)
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition aggregating six paragraphs on attorney-in-fact authority for bid bonds.

Natural_Language: Any person signing a bid bond as an attorney-in-fact must include with the bid bond evidence of authority to bind the surety.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_101_3_a: Person signing bid bond as attorney-in-fact must include evidence of authority to bind surety
Validation_Notes: Mandatory conditional: signing as attorney-in-fact triggers the evidence requirement. 'Must' indicates mandatory obligation. Rule 15 flagged.

Natural_Language: An original, or a photocopy or facsimile of an original, power of attorney is sufficient evidence of such authority.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_101_3_b_1: Original power of attorney is sufficient evidence; P_28_101_3_b_2: Photocopy of original is sufficient evidence; P_28_101_3_b_3: Facsimile of original is sufficient evidence
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive: any of the three formats satisfies the evidence requirement. Inclusive disjunction.

Natural_Language: For purposes of this section, electronic, mechanically-applied and printed signatures, seals and dates on the power of attorney must be considered original signatures, seals and dates, without regard to the order in which they were affixed.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_101_3_c_1: Electronic signatures/seals/dates must be considered original; P_28_101_3_c_2: Mechanically-applied signatures/seals/dates must be considered original; P_28_101_3_c_3: Printed signatures/seals/dates must be considered original; P_28_101_3_c_4: Order of affixing is irrelevant
Validation_Notes: Conjunctive mandate: all three signature types must be treated as original, AND order is irrelevant. The serial comma structure with 'and' confirms conjunction not disjunction.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer must- (parent aggregating (1)-(2)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_101_3_d: CO obligations regarding power of attorney as specified in (1) and (2)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating two mandatory CO obligations regarding POA treatment.

Natural_Language: Treat the failure to provide a signed and dated power of attorney at the time of bid opening as a matter of responsiveness.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_101_3_d_1: Failure to provide signed/dated POA at bid opening is a matter of responsiveness
Validation_Notes: Mandatory classification: CO must categorize this failure as responsiveness. This has significant procurement implications as responsiveness deficiencies in sealed bidding are generally non-waivable. Rule 15 flagged.

Natural_Language: Treat questions regarding the authenticity and enforceability of the power of attorney at the time of bid opening as a matter of responsibility. These questions are handled after bid opening.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_101_3_d_2_a: Questions re authenticity/enforceability of POA at bid opening are a matter of responsibility; P_28_101_3_d_2_b: These questions are handled after bid opening
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive antecedent (authenticity OR enforceability questions) triggers conjunctive consequent (classified as responsibility AND handled post-opening). Critical distinction from (d)(1): responsibility vs. responsiveness has different procedural paths.

Natural_Language: Surety validation procedures (parent aggregating (1)-(3)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_101_3_e: Surety validation procedures as specified in (1) through (3)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating three procedural scenarios for surety validation of power of attorney.

Natural_Language: If the contracting officer contacts the surety to validate the power of attorney, the contracting officer must document the file providing, at a minimum, the following information: (parent with (i)-(iii)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_101_3_e_1: If CO contacts surety to validate POA then CO must document file with minimum information per (i)-(iii)
Validation_Notes: Conditional: contacting surety triggers mandatory documentation requirement. The 'at a minimum' language means the three sub-elements are a floor not a ceiling. Conjunctive consequent: all three documentation elements required.

Natural_Language: Name of person contacted.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_101_3_e_1_i: Documentation must include name of person contacted
Validation_Notes: Atomic documentation requirement. One of three minimum elements.

Natural_Language: Date and time of contact.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_101_3_e_1_ii: Documentation must include date and time of contact
Validation_Notes: Atomic documentation requirement. One of three minimum elements.

Natural_Language: Response of the surety.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_101_3_e_1_iii: Documentation must include response of the surety
Validation_Notes: Atomic documentation requirement. One of three minimum elements.

Natural_Language: If, upon investigation, the surety declares the power of attorney to have been valid at the time of bid opening, the contracting officer may require correction of any technical error.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_101_3_e_2: If surety declares POA valid at bid opening then CO may require correction of technical error
Validation_Notes: Conditional with permissive consequent. 'May' indicates CO discretion to require or not require correction. The tautology reflects discretionary authority.

Natural_Language: If the surety declares the power of attorney to have been invalid, the contracting officer must not allow the bidder to substitute a replacement power of attorney or a replacement surety.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_101_3_e_3_a: If surety declares POA invalid then CO must not allow substitute POA; P_28_101_3_e_3_b: If surety declares POA invalid then CO must not allow replacement surety
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7
Validation_Notes: Conditional with conjunctive negative consequent. Both prohibitions are triggered simultaneously by surety declaration of invalidity. 'Must not' is mandatory prohibition. Contrasts with permissive (e)(2).

Natural_Language: Determinations of non-responsibility based on the unacceptability of a power of attorney are not subject to the Certificate of Competency process of part 19 if the surety has disavowed the validity of the power of attorney.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_101_3_f: If surety disavows POA validity then non-responsibility determination based on POA unacceptability is not subject to COC process
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Conditional with conjunctive antecedent: both surety disavowal AND non-responsibility determination based on POA must be present. Consequent is negation of COC applicability. Cross-references Part 19. Important exception to normal small business protections.

Natural_Language: Noncompliance with bid guarantee requirements (parent aggregating (a)-(c)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_101_4: Noncompliance requirements as specified in (a) through (c)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating three paragraphs: sealed bidding treatment, negotiation treatment, and mandatory waiver circumstances.

Natural_Language: In sealed bidding, noncompliance with a solicitation requirement for a bid guarantee requires rejection of the bid, except in the situations described in paragraph (c) of this subsection when the noncompliance must be waived.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_101_4_a: In sealed bidding noncompliance with bid guarantee requirement requires bid rejection except as waived in (c)
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Conditional: sealed bidding context AND noncompliance AND none of the (c) exceptions triggers mandatory rejection. The negation of (c) exceptions in the antecedent preserves the 'except' qualifier.

Natural_Language: In negotiation, noncompliance with a solicitation requirement for a bid guarantee requires rejection of an initial proposal as unacceptable, if a determination is made to award the contract based on initial proposals without discussion, except in the situations described in paragraph (c) of this subsection when noncompliance must be waived. (See part 15.) If the conditions for awarding based on initial proposals are not met, deficiencies in bid guarantees submitted by offerors determined to be in the competitive range must be addressed during discussions and the offeror must be given an opportunity to correct the deficiency.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_101_4_b_1: In negotiation noncompliance requires rejection of initial proposal if awarding without discussion except as in (c); P_28_101_4_b_2: If conditions for initial proposal award not met then deficiencies must be addressed during discussions; P_28_101_4_b_3: Offeror must be given opportunity to correct deficiency
Formal_Logic_Statement: (Negotiation ^ Noncompliance ^ Award_On_Initial ^ ~P_28_101_4_c) -> Reject_Initial_Proposal; (Negotiation ^ Noncompliance ^ ~Award_On_Initial ^ In_Competitive_Range) -> (Address_In_Discussions ^ Opportunity_To_Correct)
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Two distinct conditional paths based on award methodology. Path 1: award on initial proposals triggers rejection (with (c) exception). Path 2: when discussions required then deficiencies addressed and correction opportunity given. Cross-references Part 15 and paragraph (c). Complex logic with multiple conjunctive antecedent elements.

Natural_Language: Noncompliance with a solicitation requirement for a bid guarantee must be waived in the following circumstances unless the contracting officer determines in writing that acceptance of the bid would be detrimental to the Government's interest when- (parent aggregating (1)-(8)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_101_4_c: Noncompliance must be waived in circumstances (1)-(8) unless CO determines in writing that acceptance detrimental to Government interest
Formal_Logic_Statement: (P_28_101_4_c_1 v P_28_101_4_c_2 v P_28_101_4_c_3 v P_28_101_4_c_4 v P_28_101_4_c_5 v P_28_101_4_c_6 v P_28_101_4_c_7 v P_28_101_4_c_8) ^ ~CO_Written_Detriment_Determination -> Waive_Noncompliance
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Addition (Add): Rule 8; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Complex conditional with disjunctive antecedent (any of 8 circumstances) combined with negation of written detriment finding. The 'unless' clause creates an override: even when waiver circumstances exist the CO can prevent waiver via written determination. This is a mandatory waiver with an escape valve. Rule 15 HIGH-RISK due to the unless/override interaction.

Natural_Language: Only one offer is received. In this case, the contracting officer may require the furnishing of the bid guarantee before award.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_101_4_c_1_a: Only one offer received triggers waiver circumstance; P_28_101_4_c_1_b: CO may require bid guarantee furnishing before award
Validation_Notes: First waiver circumstance. Mandatory waiver triggered by sole offer. CO retains permissive authority to require bid guarantee before award as a condition. Two-part: trigger is mandatory while pre-award requirement is discretionary.

Natural_Language: The amount of the bid guarantee submitted is less than required, but is equal to or greater than the difference between the offer price and the next higher acceptable offer.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_101_4_c_2: Bid guarantee amount less than required but >= difference between offer price and next higher acceptable offer
Validation_Notes: Second waiver circumstance. Conjunctive antecedent: guarantee must be both (a) less than required AND (b) sufficient to cover the price differential. This protects the Government against the specific risk of the low bidder defaulting.

Natural_Language: The amount of the bid guarantee submitted, although less than that required by the solicitation for the maximum quantity offered, is sufficient for a quantity for which the offeror is otherwise eligible for award. Any award to the offeror must not exceed the quantity covered by the bid guarantee.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_101_4_c_3_a: Bid guarantee less than required for max quantity but sufficient for a lesser eligible quantity; P_28_101_4_c_3_b: Award must not exceed quantity covered by bid guarantee
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Third waiver circumstance with embedded mandatory restriction. Waiver is conditional on sufficiency for lesser quantity AND award is capped at covered quantity. The second clause is a mandatory constraint not a discretionary element.

Natural_Language: The bid guarantee is received late, and late receipt is waived under part 14.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_101_4_c_4: Bid guarantee received late AND late receipt waived under Part 14
Validation_Notes: Fourth waiver circumstance. Conjunctive antecedent: both late receipt AND Part 14 waiver must be present. Cross-references Part 14 late submission rules.

Natural_Language: A bid guarantee becomes inadequate as a result of the correction of a mistake under part 14 (but only if the bidder will increase the bid guarantee to the level required for the corrected bid).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_101_4_c_5: Bid guarantee became inadequate due to Part 14 mistake correction AND bidder will increase guarantee to required level
Validation_Notes: Fifth waiver circumstance. Conjunctive antecedent with a mandatory condition: the waiver applies only if bidder commits to increasing the guarantee. Cross-references Part 14 mistake correction.

Natural_Language: An otherwise acceptable bid bond was submitted with a signed offer, but the bid bond was not signed by the offeror.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_101_4_c_6: Otherwise acceptable bid bond submitted with signed offer but bond itself not signed by offeror
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Sixth waiver circumstance. Three conjunctive elements: bond is otherwise acceptable AND offer was signed AND bond was not signed by offeror. The deficiency is specifically the offeror signature on the bond not the offer itself.

Natural_Language: An otherwise acceptable bid bond is erroneously dated or bears no date at all.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_101_4_c_7: Otherwise acceptable bid bond is erroneously dated or undated
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Seventh waiver circumstance. Conjunctive: bond must be otherwise acceptable AND have a date deficiency. Date deficiency is disjunctive: either wrong date or no date.

Natural_Language: A bid bond does not list the United States as obligee, but correctly identifies the offeror, the solicitation number, and the name and location of the project involved, so long as it is acceptable in all other respects.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_101_4_c_8: Bid bond omits US as obligee but correctly identifies offeror and solicitation number and project name/location and is otherwise acceptable
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Eighth waiver circumstance. Five conjunctive elements: obligee omission AND four correct identifications AND general acceptability. The most complex waiver circumstance with the most conditions.

Natural_Language: Performance and payment bonds and alternative payment protections for construction contracts (parent aggregating 28.102-1 through 28.102-3).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_102: Construction contract bonding requirements as specified in 28.102-1 through 28.102-3
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating three subsections on construction bond requirements: general, amount, and clauses.

Natural_Language: General (parent aggregating (a)-(c)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_102_1: General construction bonding requirements as specified in (a) through (c)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating three paragraphs on general construction bonding.

Natural_Language: 40 U.S.C. chapter 31, subchapter III, Bonds (formerly known as the Miller Act), requires performance and payment bonds for any construction contract exceeding $150,000, except that this requirement may be waived- (parent with (1)-(2)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_102_1_a_1: Miller Act requires performance and payment bonds for construction contracts exceeding $150K; P_28_102_1_a_2: Requirement may be waived per (1) or (2)
Formal_Logic_Statement: (Construction_Contract ^ Exceeds_150K) -> (Perf_Bond_Required ^ Payment_Bond_Required); Waiver per P_28_102_1_a_1 v P_28_102_1_a_2
Validation_Notes: Statutory mandate from 40 USC ch.31. Conjunctive antecedent (construction AND >$150K) triggers conjunctive requirement (performance AND payment bonds). Waiver exceptions in sub-paragraphs. External statutory dependency.

Natural_Language: By the contracting officer for as much of the work as is to be performed in a foreign country upon finding that it is impracticable for the contractor to furnish such bonds.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_102_1_a_1: CO may waive bond requirement for foreign country work upon finding of impracticability
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7
Validation_Notes: Permissive waiver authority. Conjunctive conditions: foreign country performance AND impracticability finding. The 'may' in parent (a) ('may be waived') makes this discretionary even when conditions are met.

Natural_Language: As otherwise authorized by the Bonds statute or other law.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_102_1_a_2: Waiver authorized by Bonds statute or other law
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive waiver authority: either Bonds statute or other law. Catch-all provision preserving other legal authorities.

Natural_Language: Pursuant to 40 U.S.C. 3132, for construction contracts greater than $35,000, but not greater than $150,000, the contracting officer must select two or more of the following payment protections, giving particular consideration to inclusion of an irrevocable letter of credit as one of the selected alternatives: (parent with (1)-(2)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_102_1_b: For construction $35K-$150K CO must select 2+ payment protections with particular consideration to ILC
Validation_Notes: Statutory requirement from 40 USC 3132. Three conjunctive antecedent conditions trigger conjunctive obligation: select 2+ protections AND give particular consideration to ILC. The 'particular consideration' to ILC is advisory weight not a mandate to select it.

Natural_Language: Payment protection options (parent listing (i)-(v)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_102_1_b_1: Five payment protection options available for CO selection
Validation_Notes: Parent listing five disjunctive options. CO must select 2+ from this list per parent (b). Options are disjunctive but per parent at least two must be selected.

Natural_Language: A payment bond.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_102_1_b_1_i: Payment bond is an available payment protection option
Validation_Notes: Atomic option. One of five payment protection alternatives.

Natural_Language: An irrevocable letter of credit (ILC).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_102_1_b_1_ii: Irrevocable letter of credit is an available payment protection option
Validation_Notes: Atomic option. Per parent (b) this option receives particular consideration.

Natural_Language: A tripartite escrow agreement. The prime contractor establishes an escrow account in a federally insured financial institution and enters into a tripartite escrow agreement with the financial institution, as escrow agent, and all of the suppliers of labor and material. The escrow agreement must establish the terms of payment under the contract and of resolution of disputes among the parties. The Government makes payments to the contractor's escrow account, and the escrow agent distributes the payments in accordance with the agreement, or triggers the disputes resolution procedures if required.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_102_1_b_1_iii_a: Prime contractor establishes escrow account in federally insured institution; P_28_102_1_b_1_iii_b: Tripartite agreement with institution and all suppliers; P_28_102_1_b_1_iii_c: Agreement must establish payment terms and dispute resolution; P_28_102_1_b_1_iii_d: Government pays to escrow account; P_28_102_1_b_1_iii_e: Escrow agent distributes per agreement or triggers dispute resolution
Validation_Notes: Complex atomic option with five conjunctive implementation requirements. All elements must be present for a valid tripartite escrow arrangement.

Natural_Language: Certificates of deposit. The contractor deposits certificates of deposit from a federally insured financial institution with the contracting officer, in an acceptable form, executable by the contracting officer.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_102_1_b_1_iv_a: Contractor deposits CDs from federally insured institution; P_28_102_1_b_1_iv_b: CDs in acceptable form; P_28_102_1_b_1_iv_c: CDs executable by CO
Validation_Notes: Atomic option with three conjunctive requirements for valid CD submission.

Natural_Language: A deposit of the types of security listed in 28.204-1 and 28.204-2.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_102_1_b_1_v: Deposit of security types per 28.204-1 and 28.204-2 is an available option
Validation_Notes: Atomic option cross-referencing 28.204-1 (US bonds/notes) and 28.204-2 (checks/drafts/money orders/currency).

Natural_Language: The contractor must submit to the Government one of the payment protections selected by the contracting officer.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_102_1_b_2: Contractor must submit one of the CO-selected payment protections
Validation_Notes: Mandatory obligation on contractor. CO selects the menu; contractor picks one from that menu and submits it. Sequential dependency on CO's selection under (b)(1).

Natural_Language: The contractor must furnish all bonds or alternative payment protection, including any necessary reinsurance agreements, before receiving a notice to proceed with the work or being allowed to start work.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_102_1_c_a: Contractor must furnish all bonds/protections including reinsurance before NTP; P_28_102_1_c_b: Contractor must furnish all before being allowed to start work
Validation_Notes: Temporal mandate: furnishing must precede both NTP and work start. The 'or' between NTP and being allowed to start indicates whichever comes first. Mandatory sequencing requirement.

Natural_Language: Amount required (parent aggregating (a)-(e)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_102_2: Bond/protection amount requirements as specified in (a) through (e)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating five paragraphs on amount determination for construction bonds.

Natural_Language: Definition. As used in this subsection- Original contract price means the award price of the contract; or, for requirements contracts, the price payable for the estimated total quantity; or, for indefinite-quantity contracts, the price payable for the specified minimum quantity. Original contract price does not include the price of any options, except those options exercised at the time of contract award.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_102_2_a_1: Original contract price = award price; P_28_102_2_a_2: For requirements contracts = price for estimated total quantity; P_28_102_2_a_3: For indefinite-quantity contracts = price for specified minimum quantity; P_28_102_2_a_4: Excludes options except those exercised at award
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive definition based on contract type (fixed-price vs requirements vs IDIQ) combined conjunctively with universal options exclusion. The three definitions are mutually exclusive by contract type. Options exclusion applies across all types.

Natural_Language: Contracts exceeding $150,000 (parent aggregating (1)-(2)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_102_2_b: Bond amounts for contracts >$150K as specified in (1) and (2)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating performance bond and payment bond amount requirements for >$150K contracts.

Natural_Language: Performance bonds. Unless the contracting officer determines that a lesser amount is adequate for the protection of the Government, the penal amount of performance bonds must equal- (parent with (i)-(ii)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_102_2_b_1: Performance bond penal amount requirements unless CO determines lesser amount adequate
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7
Validation_Notes: Default rule with CO override. Unless CO makes lesser-amount determination the full amount requirements in (i) and (ii) apply. Negation of CO determination triggers mandatory conjunctive requirements.

Natural_Language: 100 percent of the original contract price.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_102_2_b_1_i: Performance bond penal amount must equal 100% of original contract price
Validation_Notes: Atomic amount requirement. Base performance bond amount.

Natural_Language: If the contract price increases, an additional amount equal to 100 percent of the increase.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_102_2_b_1_ii: If contract price increases then additional performance bond amount = 100% of increase
Validation_Notes: Conditional triggered by price increase. Mandatory additional bonding at 100% of the increase amount. Ensures performance bond remains proportional throughout contract life.

Natural_Language: Payment bonds (parent with (i)-(ii)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_102_2_b_2: Payment bond amount requirements for >$150K contracts as specified in (i) and (ii)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating payment bond amount requirements and the performance bond floor.

Natural_Language: Unless the contracting officer makes a written determination supported by specific findings that a payment bond in this amount is impractical, the amount of the payment bond must equal- (parent with (A)-(B)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_102_2_b_2_i: Unless CO makes written impracticability determination with specific findings payment bond must equal amounts in (A)-(B)
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7
Validation_Notes: Default rule with CO override requiring written determination with specific findings. Higher documentation burden than performance bond override in (b)(1) which requires only a determination. Negation of override triggers mandatory amounts.

Natural_Language: 100 percent of the original contract price.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_102_2_b_2_i_A: Payment bond must equal 100% of original contract price
Validation_Notes: Atomic amount requirement. Base payment bond amount. Parallel to performance bond requirement at (b)(1)(i).

Natural_Language: If the contract price increases, an additional amount equal to 100 percent of the increase.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_102_2_b_2_i_B: If contract price increases then additional payment bond = 100% of increase
Validation_Notes: Conditional triggered by price increase. Parallel to performance bond increase at (b)(1)(ii).

Natural_Language: The amount of the payment bond must be no less than the amount of the performance bond.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_102_2_b_2_ii: Payment bond amount >= performance bond amount
Validation_Notes: Floor constraint: payment bond cannot be less than performance bond. This means if CO reduces performance bond under (b)(1) override the payment bond floor adjusts accordingly.

Natural_Language: Contracts exceeding $35,000 but not exceeding $150,000. Unless the contracting officer determines that a lesser amount is adequate for the protection of the Government, the penal amount of the payment bond or the amount of alternative payment protection must equal- (parent with (1)-(2)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_102_2_c: For $35K-$150K contracts bond/protection amount requirements unless CO determines lesser adequate
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Parallel structure to (b) but for the $35K-$150K tier. Same CO override mechanism. Applies to both payment bonds and alternative payment protections.

Natural_Language: 100 percent of the original contract price.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_102_2_c_1: Penal amount must equal 100% of original contract price
Validation_Notes: Atomic amount requirement for $35K-$150K tier. Same 100% standard as >$150K tier.

Natural_Language: If the contract price increases, an additional amount equal to 100 percent of the increase.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_102_2_c_2: If price increases then additional amount = 100% of increase
Validation_Notes: Conditional triggered by price increase for $35K-$150K tier. Same structure as higher tier.

Natural_Language: Securing additional payment protection. If the contract price increases, the Government must secure any needed additional protection by directing the contractor to- (parent with (1)-(3)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_102_2_d: If price increases Government must secure additional protection via one of three methods
Validation_Notes: Conditional with disjunctive consequent. Price increase triggers mandatory action but Government has choice of three methods. 'Must' makes action mandatory; three options provide flexibility in method.

Natural_Language: Increase the penal sum of the existing bond.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_102_2_d_1: Direct contractor to increase penal sum of existing bond
Validation_Notes: Atomic option. First of three methods for securing additional protection.

Natural_Language: Obtain an additional bond.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_102_2_d_2: Direct contractor to obtain an additional bond
Validation_Notes: Atomic option. Second method.

Natural_Language: Furnish additional alternative payment protection.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_102_2_d_3: Direct contractor to furnish additional alternative payment protection
Validation_Notes: Atomic option. Third method.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer may reduce the amount of security to support a bond, subject to the conditions of 28.203-3(c) or 28.204(b).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_102_2_e: CO may reduce security amount subject to conditions of 28.203-3(c) or 28.204(b)
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Permissive authority conditioned on meeting one of two cross-referenced conditions. Disjunctive trigger (either condition set) with tautological consequent reflecting discretion. Cross-references 28.203-3(c) and 28.204(b).

Natural_Language: Contract clauses (parent aggregating (a)-(b)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_102_3: Construction contract clause requirements as specified in (a) and (b)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating two clause insertion requirements for construction contracts at different thresholds.

Natural_Language: Insert a clause substantially the same as the clause at 52.228-15, Performance and Payment Bonds - Construction, in solicitations and contracts for construction that contain a requirement for performance and payment bonds if the resultant contract is expected to exceed $150,000. The contracting officer may revise paragraphs (b)(1) and/or (b)(2) of the clause to establish a lower percentage in accordance with 28.102-2(b). If the provision at 52.228-1 is not included in the solicitation, the contracting officer must set a period of time for return of executed bonds.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_102_3_a_1: Insert 52.228-15 in construction solicitations/contracts with perf/payment bond requirement when >$150K; P_28_102_3_a_2: CO may revise clause percentages per 28.102-2(b); P_28_102_3_a_3: If 52.228-1 not included CO must set bond return period
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Three-part provision: mandatory clause insertion conditional on threshold; permissive percentage revision; and conditional bond return period requirement when 52.228-1 absent. Multiple cross-references.

Natural_Language: Insert the clause at 52.228-13, Alternative Payment Protections, in solicitations and contracts for construction, when the estimated or actual value exceeds $35,000 but does not exceed $150,000. Complete the clause by specifying the payment protections selected (see 28.102-1(b)(1)) and the deadline for submission. The contracting officer may revise paragraph (b) of the clause to establish a lower percentage in accordance with 28.102-2(c).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_102_3_b_1: Insert 52.228-13 for construction when $35K-$150K; P_28_102_3_b_2: Specify selected payment protections and submission deadline; P_28_102_3_b_3: CO may revise clause percentage per 28.102-2(c)
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Mandatory clause insertion for mid-tier construction with conjunctive completion requirements. Permissive percentage revision. Cross-references 28.102-1(b)(1) and 28.102-2(c).

Natural_Language: Performance and payment bonds for other than construction contracts (parent aggregating 28.103-1 through 28.103-4).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_103: Non-construction bonding requirements as specified in 28.103-1 through 28.103-4
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating four subsections on non-construction bonding.

Natural_Language: General (parent aggregating (a)-(c)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_103_1: General non-construction bonding requirements as specified in (a) through (c)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating three general policy paragraphs for non-construction bonds.

Natural_Language: Generally, agencies must not require performance and payment bonds for other than construction contracts. However, performance and payment bonds may be used as permitted in 28.103-2 and 28.103-3.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_103_1_a_1: Agencies must not require performance/payment bonds for non-construction generally; P_28_103_1_a_2: Performance/payment bonds may be used as permitted in 28.103-2 and 28.103-3
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Default prohibition with permissive exceptions. The general rule is no bonds for non-construction. Cross-references 28.103-2 and 28.103-3 create exceptions. The 'However' signals the permissive carve-out.

Natural_Language: The contractor must furnish all bonds before receiving a notice to proceed with the work.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_103_1_b: Contractor must furnish all bonds before NTP
Validation_Notes: Temporal mandate parallel to 28.102-1(c) but for non-construction. Bonds must precede NTP.

Natural_Language: No bond must be required after the contract has been awarded if it was not specifically required in the contract, except as may be determined necessary for a contract modification.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_103_1_c_1: No bond required after award if not in contract; P_28_103_1_c_2: Exception for contract modifications where bond determined necessary
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Prohibition with exception. Default is no post-award bond requirement unless it was in the contract. Modification exception creates a narrow permissive carve-out. Three conjunctive antecedent elements with the modification exception negated.

Natural_Language: Performance bonds (parent aggregating (a)-(c)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_103_2: Non-construction performance bond requirements as specified in (a) through (c)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating three paragraphs on non-construction performance bonds.

Natural_Language: Performance bonds may be required for contracts exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold when necessary to protect the Government's interest. The following situations may warrant a performance bond: (parent listing (1)-(4)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_103_2_a: Performance bonds may be required for contracts >SAT when necessary; four illustrative situations listed
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7
Validation_Notes: Permissive authority with two conjunctive prerequisites: exceeding SAT and necessity for Government protection. The four situations in (1)-(4) are illustrative not exhaustive per 'may warrant' language.

Natural_Language: Government property or funds are to be provided to the contractor for use in performing the contract or as partial compensation (as in retention of salvaged material).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_103_2_a_1: Government property or funds provided to contractor for performance or as partial compensation
Validation_Notes: Illustrative situation warranting performance bond. Atomic proposition.

Natural_Language: A contractor sells assets to or merges with another concern, and the Government, after recognizing the latter concern as the successor in interest, desires assurance that it is financially capable.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_103_2_a_2: Contractor sells/merges and Government desires financial capability assurance from successor
Validation_Notes: Illustrative situation. Three conjunctive conditions: transaction occurred AND successor recognized AND Government desires assurance.

Natural_Language: Substantial progress payments are made before delivery of end items starts.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_103_2_a_3: Substantial progress payments made before end item delivery begins
Validation_Notes: Illustrative situation. Atomic proposition identifying financial risk to Government.

Natural_Language: Contracts are for dismantling, demolition, or removal of improvements.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_103_2_a_4: Contract involves dismantling or demolition or removal of improvements
Validation_Notes: Illustrative situation. Disjunctive: any of three work types qualifies.

Natural_Language: The Government may require additional performance bond protection when a contract price is increased.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_103_2_b: Government may require additional performance bond when price increases
Validation_Notes: Permissive authority. Price increase triggers discretionary ability to require additional bond. 'May' = not mandatory.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer must determine the contractor's responsibility (see part 9) even though a bond has been or can be obtained.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_103_2_c: CO must determine contractor responsibility regardless of bond status
Validation_Notes: Mandatory obligation independent of bond status. Bond does not substitute for responsibility determination. Critical procurement principle: bonding and responsibility are separate assessments. Cross-references Part 9.

Natural_Language: Payment bonds (parent aggregating (a)-(b)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_103_3: Non-construction payment bond requirements as specified in (a) and (b)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating two paragraphs on non-construction payment bonds.

Natural_Language: A payment bond is required only when a performance bond is required, and if the use of payment bond is in the Government's interest.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_103_3_a: Payment bond required only when performance bond required AND in Government interest
Validation_Notes: Near-biconditional: 'only when' plus conjunctive condition. Payment bond cannot exist without performance bond AND Government interest finding. The 'only when' language strongly suggests biconditional but technically is one-directional ('required only when'). Marked PENDING_REVIEW for biconditional vs implication judgment call.

Natural_Language: When a contract price is increased, the Government may require additional bond protection in an amount adequate to protect suppliers of labor and material.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_103_3_b: Government may require additional payment bond protection when price increases
Validation_Notes: Permissive authority parallel to 28.103-2(b). Price increase triggers discretionary additional protection. Amount must be adequate to protect labor/material suppliers.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer must insert a clause substantially the same as the clause at 52.228-16, Performance and Payment Bonds - Other than Construction, in solicitations and contracts that contain a requirement for both payment and performance bonds. The contracting officer must determine the amount of each bond for insertion in the clause. The amount must be adequate to protect the interest of the Government. The contracting officer must also set a period of time (normally 10 days) for return of executed bonds. Alternate I must be used when only performance bonds are required.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_103_4_a: Insert 52.228-16 when both payment and performance bonds required; P_28_103_4_b: CO must determine amount of each bond; P_28_103_4_c: Amount must be adequate to protect Government; P_28_103_4_d: CO must set bond return period (normally 10 days); P_28_103_4_e: Alternate I when only performance bonds required
Formal_Logic_Statement: (Payment_Bond ^ Perf_Bond) -> (Insert_52_228_16 ^ Determine_Amounts ^ Adequate_Protection ^ Set_Return_Period); Only_Perf_Bond -> Use_Alternate_I
Validation_Notes: Multi-requirement provision. Primary conditional with four conjunctive obligations. Secondary conditional for Alternate I usage. The 'normally 10 days' is advisory guidance not a hard requirement. Cross-references 52.228-16.

Natural_Language: Annual performance bonds (parent aggregating (a)-(b)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_104: Annual performance bond requirements as specified in (a) and (b)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating two paragraphs on annual performance bonds.

Natural_Language: Annual performance bonds only apply to nonconstruction contracts. They must provide a gross penal sum applicable to the total amount of all covered contracts.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_104_a_1: Annual performance bonds apply only to nonconstruction contracts; P_28_104_a_2: Must provide gross penal sum covering total amount of all covered contracts
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Two conjunctive requirements: nonconstruction restriction AND gross penal sum coverage. The 'only' makes the first element restrictive.

Natural_Language: When the penal sums obligated by contracts are approximately equal to or exceed the penal sum of the annual performance bond, an additional bond will be required to cover additional contracts.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_104_b: When obligated penal sums approach or exceed annual bond penal sum then additional bond required
Validation_Notes: Conditional mandate. 'Will be required' is mandatory. Triggered when accumulated obligations exhaust the annual bond capacity. Note 'approximately equal to' introduces judgment in the trigger threshold.

Natural_Language: Other types of bonds. The head of the contracting activity may approve using other types of bonds in connection with acquiring particular supplies or services. These types include advance payment bonds and patent infringement bonds.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_105: HCA may approve other bond types for particular supplies/services
Validation_Notes: Permissive authority at HCA level. Advance payment and patent infringement bonds are illustrative. Parent aggregating 28.105-1 and 28.105-2.

Natural_Language: Advance payment bonds may be required only when the contract contains an advance payment provision and a performance bond is not furnished. The contracting officer must determine the amount of the advance payment bond necessary to protect the Government.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_105_1_a: Advance payment bonds may be required only when advance payment provision exists AND no performance bond furnished; P_28_105_1_b: CO must determine amount necessary to protect Government
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Two-part provision. First: permissive requirement conditioned on conjunctive antecedent (advance payment provision AND no performance bond). Second: mandatory amount determination when bond is required.

Natural_Language: Patent infringement bonds (parent aggregating (a)-(b)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_105_2: Patent infringement bond requirements as specified in (a) and (b)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating conditions for requiring patent infringement bonds and CO's penal sum determination obligation.

Natural_Language: Contracts providing for patent indemnity may require these bonds only if- (parent with (1)-(2)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_105_2_a: Patent infringement bonds may be required only if both conditions in (1) and (2) met
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Permissive requirement with conjunctive conditions. Patent indemnity contract AND both sub-conditions must be met. 'Only if' makes conditions necessary but not sufficient due to 'may'.

Natural_Language: A performance bond is not furnished.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_105_2_a_1: Performance bond not furnished
Validation_Notes: Atomic condition. First prerequisite for patent infringement bond. Simple negation.

Natural_Language: The financial responsibility of the contractor is unknown or doubtful.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_105_2_a_2: Contractor financial responsibility unknown or doubtful
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive condition. Second prerequisite for patent infringement bond. Either unknown or doubtful suffices.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer must determine the penal sum.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_105_2_b: CO must determine patent infringement bond penal sum
Validation_Notes: Mandatory obligation on CO. No formula or percentage specified; left to CO judgment. Triggered when patent infringement bond is required.

Natural_Language: Substitution of surety bonds (parent aggregating (a)-(b)).

Natural_Language: A new surety bond covering all or part of the obligations on a bond previously approved may be substituted for the original bond if approved by the head of the contracting activity, or as otherwise specified in agency regulation.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_106_2_a: New surety bond may substitute for original if HCA approves or per agency regulation
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Permissive authority with disjunctive authorization sources: HCA approval OR agency regulation. 'May' indicates discretion even when authorization exists. Bond can cover all or part of original obligations.

Natural_Language: When a new surety bond is approved, the contracting officer must notify the principal and surety of the original bond of the effective date of the new bond.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_106_2_b: When new bond approved CO must notify original principal and surety of effective date
Validation_Notes: Mandatory notification triggered by bond approval. Three conjunctive elements: notify principal AND notify surety AND provide effective date.

Natural_Language: Additional bond and security (parent aggregating (a)-(b)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_106_3: Additional bond and security form requirements as specified in (a) and (b)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating two form-usage scenarios for additional bond coverage.

Natural_Language: When additional bond coverage is required and is secured in whole or in part by the original surety or sureties, agencies must use Standard Form 1415, Consent of Surety and Increase of Penalty.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_106_3_a: When additional coverage secured by original surety then use SF 1415
Validation_Notes: Conditional mandate: conjunctive antecedent (additional coverage needed AND original surety involved) triggers mandatory SF 1415 usage.

Natural_Language: When additional bond coverage is required and is secured in whole or in part by a new surety or by one of the alternatives described in 28.204 in lieu of corporate or individual surety, agencies must use Standard Form 25, Performance Bond; Standard Form 1418, Performance Bond for Other Than Construction Contracts; Standard Form 25A, Payment Bond; or Standard Form 1416, Payment Bond for Other Than Construction Contracts.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_106_3_b: When additional coverage by new surety or 28.204 alternative then use appropriate SF (25/1418/25A/1416)
Formal_Logic_Statement: (Additional_Coverage_Required ^ (New_Surety v Alternative_28_204)) -> (Use_SF_25 v Use_SF_1418 v Use_SF_25A v Use_SF_1416)
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Conditional with disjunctive antecedent element (new surety OR 28.204 alternative) and disjunctive consequent (choice of four forms depending on bond type and contract type). Cross-references 28.204.

Natural_Language: Contract clause (parent aggregating (a)-(b)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_106_4: Bond-related contract clause requirements as specified in (a) and (b)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating two clause insertion requirements.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer must insert the clause at 52.228-2, Additional Bond Security, in solicitations and contracts when bonds are required.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_106_4_a: CO must insert 52.228-2 when bonds required
Validation_Notes: Mandatory clause insertion conditional on bonds being required. Cross-references 52.228-2.

Natural_Language: In accordance with section 806(a)(3) of Public Law 102-190, as amended by sections 2091 and 8105 of Public Law 103-355 (10 U.S.C. 4601 note prec.), the contracting officer must insert the clause at 52.228-12, Prospective Subcontractor Requests for Bonds, in solicitations and contracts with respect to which a payment bond will be furnished pursuant to 40 U.S.C. chapter 31, subchapter III, Bonds (see 28.102-1), except for contracts for the acquisition of commercial products or commercial services as defined in part 2.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_106_4_b_1: CO must insert 52.228-12 when payment bond furnished under Bonds statute; P_28_106_4_b_2: Exception for commercial product/service contracts
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Statutory mandate from Pub.L.102-190. Conjunctive antecedent: payment bond under Bonds statute AND not commercial. Cross-references 28.102-1 and Part 2. External statutory dependency on 10 USC 4601.

Natural_Language: Consent of surety (parent aggregating (a)-(c)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_106_5: Consent of surety requirements as specified in (a) through (c)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating three paragraphs on when consent of surety is/is not required and prescribed form.

Natural_Language: When any contract is modified, the contracting officer must obtain the consent of surety if- (parent with (1)-(3)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_106_5_a: Contract modification triggers consent of surety requirement under conditions (1)-(3)
Formal_Logic_Statement: Contract_Modified ^ (P_28_106_5_a_1 v P_28_106_5_a_2 v P_28_106_5_a_3) -> Obtain_Consent_of_Surety
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Conditional with conjunctive-disjunctive antecedent: contract modification AND any of three circumstances. 'Must' makes consent mandatory when triggered.

Natural_Language: An additional bond is obtained from other than the original surety.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_106_5_a_1: Additional bond obtained from non-original surety
Validation_Notes: First consent trigger. Atomic condition.

Natural_Language: No additional bond is required and- (parent with (i)-(ii)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_106_5_a_2: No additional bond required and one of two modification conditions met
Justification_Rules: Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Addition (Add): Rule 8; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7
Validation_Notes: Second consent trigger with conjunctive conditions: no additional bond AND one of two modification characteristics.

Natural_Language: The modification is for new work beyond the scope of the original contract.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_106_5_a_2_i: Modification is for new work beyond original contract scope
Validation_Notes: First sub-condition under (a)(2). Scope change triggers consent requirement.

Natural_Language: The modification does not change the contract scope but changes the contract price (upward or downward) by more than 25 percent or $50,000.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_106_5_a_2_ii_a: Modification does not change scope; P_28_106_5_a_2_ii_b: Price changes by >25% or >$50K
Justification_Rules: Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Second sub-condition under (a)(2). Conjunctive: no scope change AND price exceeds either threshold. Price thresholds are disjunctive (either >25% OR >$50K triggers). Covers both upward and downward changes.

Natural_Language: Consent of surety is required for a novation agreement (see part 42).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_106_5_a_3: Novation agreement requires consent of surety
Validation_Notes: Third consent trigger. Cross-references Part 42 (novation). Mandatory consent regardless of other conditions.

Natural_Language: When a contract for which performance or payment is secured by any of the types of security listed in 28.204 is modified as described in paragraph (a) of this subsection, no consent of surety is required.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_106_5_b: When secured by 28.204 types and modified per (a) then no consent of surety required
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Exception to (a). When alternative security used instead of surety bond there is no surety to consent. Conjunctive antecedent with negative consequent. Cross-references 28.204.

Natural_Language: Agencies must use Standard Form 1414, Consent of Surety, for all types of contracts.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_106_5_c: SF 1414 must be used for consent of surety across all contract types
Validation_Notes: Mandatory form prescription. Universal application across all contract types. No exceptions stated.

Natural_Language: Furnishing information (parent aggregating (a)-(d)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_106_6: Information furnishing requirements as specified in (a) through (d)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating four paragraphs on information disclosure obligations regarding bonds.

Natural_Language: The surety on the bond, upon its written request, may be furnished information on the progress of the work, payments, and the estimated percentage of completion, concerning the contract for which the bond was furnished.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_106_6_a: Upon surety written request surety may be furnished progress/payment/completion information
Validation_Notes: Permissive information sharing. 'May be furnished' indicates Government discretion. Triggered by surety's written request. Information categories: progress, payments, estimated completion.

Natural_Language: When a payment bond has been provided, the contracting officer must, upon request, furnish the name and address of the surety or sureties to any subcontractor or supplier who has furnished or been requested to furnish labor or material for the contract. In addition, general information concerning the work progress, payments, and the estimated percentage of completion may be furnished to persons who have provided labor or materials and have not been paid.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_106_6_b_1: When payment bond exists CO must furnish surety name/address to subs/suppliers on request; P_28_106_6_b_2: General progress/payment/completion info may be furnished to unpaid labor/material providers
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Two-part provision. First: mandatory disclosure of surety identity on request (must). Second: permissive disclosure of general info to unpaid providers (may). Different obligation levels for different information types.

Natural_Language: When a payment bond has been provided for a contract, the head of the agency or designee must furnish a certified copy of the bond and the contract for which it was given to any person who makes a request therefor and who furnishes an affidavit that the requestor has supplied labor or materials for such work and payment therefor has not been made or that the requestor is being sued on such bond. The person who makes the request must be required to pay such costs of preparation as determined by the head of the agency or designee to be reasonable and appropriate (see 40 U.S.C. 3133).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_106_6_c_1: Agency head must furnish certified copy of payment bond and contract upon request with affidavit; P_28_106_6_c_2: Requestor must pay reasonable preparation costs
Validation_Notes: Mandatory disclosure with conditions. Requestor must provide affidavit establishing either unpaid labor/materials OR being sued on the bond (disjunctive basis for request). Cost recovery is mandatory. External statutory reference: 40 USC 3133.

Natural_Language: Section 806(a)(2) of Public Law 102-190, as amended, requires that the Federal Government provide information to subcontractors on payment bonds under contracts for other than commercial products or commercial services as defined in part 2. Upon the written or oral request of a subcontractor/supplier, or prospective subcontractor/supplier, under a contract with respect to which a payment bond has been furnished pursuant to the Bonds statute, the contracting officer must promptly provide to the requester, either orally or in writing, as appropriate, any of the following: (parent with (1)-(3)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_106_6_d: Statutory requirement to provide payment bond info to subs upon request for non-commercial contracts
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Statutory mandate from Pub.L.102-190. Three conjunctive prerequisites: Bonds statute payment bond AND non-commercial AND request. Request can be written or oral. Response can be oral or written. Cross-references Part 2 commercial definitions.

Natural_Language: Name and address of the surety or sureties on the payment bond.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_106_6_d_1: CO must provide surety name and address
Validation_Notes: First mandatory disclosure item under (d).

Natural_Language: Penal amount of the payment bond.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_106_6_d_2: CO must provide penal amount of payment bond
Validation_Notes: Second mandatory disclosure item under (d).

Natural_Language: Copy of the payment bond. The contracting officer may impose reasonable fees to cover the cost of copying and providing a copy of the payment bond.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_106_6_d_3_a: CO must provide copy of payment bond; P_28_106_6_d_3_b: CO may impose reasonable copying fees
