Validation_Notes: Third mandatory disclosure item with permissive fee authority. Copy provision is mandatory; fee imposition is discretionary.

Natural_Language: Withholding contract payments (parent aggregating (a)-(c)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_106_7: Payment withholding requirements as specified in (a) through (c)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating three paragraphs on payment withholding rules.

Natural_Language: During contract performance, agencies must not withhold payments due contractors or assignees because subcontractors or suppliers have not been paid.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_106_7_a: Agencies must not withhold contractor payments due to unpaid subs/suppliers
Validation_Notes: Prohibition against withholding during performance. Protects privity of contract: Government pays contractor regardless of subcontractor payment status. Important distinction from post-completion rules in (b).

Natural_Language: If, after completion of the contract work, the Government receives written notice from the surety regarding the contractor's failure to meet its obligation to its subcontractors or suppliers, the contracting officer must withhold final payment. However, the surety must agree to hold the Government harmless from any liability resulting from withholding the final payment. The contracting officer will authorize final payment upon agreement between the contractor and surety or upon a judicial determination of the rights of the parties.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_106_7_b_1: After completion if surety provides written notice of contractor failure CO must withhold final payment; P_28_106_7_b_2: Surety must hold Government harmless from withholding liability; P_28_106_7_b_3: Final payment authorized upon contractor-surety agreement or judicial determination
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Two conditionals. First: post-completion surety notice triggers mandatory withholding with mandatory hold-harmless. Second: release of withheld payment requires either agreement or judicial determination (disjunctive). Complex interaction between mandatory withholding and conditions for release.

Natural_Language: For any withholding incident to the labor standards provisions of the contract, see part 22.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_106_7_c: Labor standards withholding governed by Part 22
Validation_Notes: Cross-reference to Part 22 for labor standards withholding. Carves out labor standards from the general withholding rules in (a) and (b). External dependency on Part 22.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer will only authorize payment to subcontractors or suppliers from an ILC (or any other cash equivalent security) upon a judicial determination of the rights of the parties, a signed notarized statement by the contractor that the payment is due and owed, or a signed agreement between the parties as to amount due and owed.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_106_8_a: CO authorizes ILC payment to subs only upon judicial determination; P_28_106_8_b: Or upon signed notarized contractor statement that payment due; P_28_106_8_c: Or upon signed agreement between parties on amount due
Validation_Notes: Restrictive authorization: payment from ILC or cash equivalent only under one of three disjunctive conditions. 'Only' language creates a necessary condition set. Any of the three bases is sufficient. Protects ILC funds from unauthorized disbursement.

Natural_Language: This subpart prescribes procedures for the use of sureties and other security to protect the Government from financial losses.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_200: Subpart 28.2 prescribes procedures for sureties and other security to protect Government from financial losses
Validation_Notes: Scope statement for Subpart 28.2. Atomic declarative proposition.

Natural_Language: Requirements for security (parent aggregating (a)-(b)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_201: Security requirements as specified in (a) and (b)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating two paragraphs on security requirements and solicitation restrictions.

Natural_Language: Agencies must obtain adequate security for bonds (including coinsurance and reinsurance agreements) required or used with a contract for supplies or services (including construction). Acceptable forms of security include- (parent with (1)-(2)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_201_a: Agencies must obtain adequate security for bonds including coinsurance/reinsurance
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Mandatory security requirement triggered by bond usage. Two disjunctive forms of acceptable security. 'Must' = mandatory. Scope includes all contract types including construction.

Natural_Language: Corporate or individual sureties.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_201_a_1: Corporate or individual sureties are acceptable security
Validation_Notes: First acceptable security form. Disjunctive: either type suffices.

Natural_Language: Any of the types of security authorized in lieu of sureties by 28.204.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_201_a_2: Security types authorized by 28.204 are acceptable
Validation_Notes: Second acceptable security form. Cross-references 28.204 alternatives.

Natural_Language: Solicitations must not preclude offerors from using the types of surety or other security permitted by this subpart, unless prohibited by law or regulation.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_201_b: Solicitations must not preclude permitted surety/security types unless prohibited by law/regulation
Validation_Notes: Prohibition against restrictive solicitation practices. Default is open access to all permitted security types. Law/regulation override is the only exception. Protects offeror flexibility.

Natural_Language: Acceptability of corporate sureties (parent aggregating (a)-(d)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_202: Corporate surety acceptability as specified in (a) through (d)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating four paragraphs on corporate surety requirements.

Natural_Language: Corporate surety requirements (parent aggregating (1)-(4)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_202_a: Corporate surety domestic requirements as specified in (1) through (4)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating four domestic corporate surety requirements.

Natural_Language: Corporate sureties offered for bonds furnished with contracts performed in the United States or its outlying areas must appear on the list contained in the Department of the Treasury's Listing of Approved Sureties (Treasury Department Circular 570).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_202_a_1: Corporate sureties for US-performed contracts must appear on Treasury Circular 570
Validation_Notes: Mandatory eligibility requirement. Conjunctive antecedent: corporate surety AND US performance. Treasury Circular 570 is the authoritative listing. External dependency on Treasury Department.

Natural_Language: The penal amount of the bond should not exceed the surety's underwriting limit stated in the Treasury Department Circular 570. If the penal amount exceeds the underwriting limit, the bond will be acceptable only if- (parent with (i)-(ii)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_202_a_2: Penal amount should not exceed underwriting limit; if exceeds then acceptable only if (i) and (ii) met
Validation_Notes: Advisory default ('should') with mandatory conditional when exceeded. If penal amount exceeds limit then both sub-conditions must be satisfied conjunctively. Note 'should' in first clause is advisory but 'only if' in second is mandatory.

Natural_Language: The amount which exceeds the specified limit is coinsured or reinsured.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_202_a_2_i: Excess amount must be coinsured or reinsured
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive requirement: either coinsurance or reinsurance covers the excess.

Natural_Language: The amount of coinsurance or reinsurance does not exceed the underwriting limit of each coinsurer or reinsurer.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_202_a_2_ii: Coinsurance/reinsurance amount must not exceed each co/reinsurer underwriting limit
Validation_Notes: Negative constraint: prevents cascading excess. Each entity in the chain must stay within its own underwriting limit.

Natural_Language: Coinsurance or reinsurance agreements must conform to the Department of the Treasury (Treasury) regulations in 31 CFR 223.10 and 223.11. When reinsurance is contemplated, the contracting office generally must require reinsurance agreements to be executed and submitted with the bonds before making a final determination on the bonds.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_202_a_3_a: Coinsurance/reinsurance must conform to 31 CFR 223.10 and 223.11; P_28_202_a_3_b: When reinsurance contemplated agreements generally must be executed and submitted with bonds before final determination
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Two requirements. First: mandatory regulatory conformance. Second: timing requirement for reinsurance submission. 'Generally' in second clause softens the mandate slightly but does not eliminate it. External regulatory dependency on 31 CFR.

Natural_Language: When specified in the solicitation, the contracting officer may accept a bond from the direct writing company in satisfaction of the total bond requirement of the contract. This is permissible until necessary reinsurance agreements are executed, even though the total bond requirement may exceed the insurer's underwriting limitation. The contractor must execute and submit necessary reinsurance agreements to the contracting officer within the time specified on the bid form, which may not exceed 45 calendar days after the execution of the bond. The contractor must use SF 273, SF 274, and SF 275 as applicable.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_202_a_4_a: When solicitation specifies CO may accept direct writing company bond pending reinsurance; P_28_202_a_4_b: Contractor must submit reinsurance within bid form time not exceeding 45 days; P_28_202_a_4_c: Must use SF 273 SF 274 SF 275 as applicable
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7
Validation_Notes: Permissive acceptance authority followed by mandatory contractor obligations. CO discretion to accept pending reinsurance; contractor then has hard 45-day deadline and mandatory form requirements. Cross-references SF 273, 274, 275.

Natural_Language: For contracts performed in a foreign country, sureties not appearing on Treasury Department Circular 570 are acceptable if the contracting officer determines that it is impracticable for the contractor to use Treasury listed sureties.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_202_b: For foreign country contracts non-Circular 570 sureties acceptable if CO determines impracticable to use listed sureties
Validation_Notes: Exception to Circular 570 requirement for foreign performance. Conjunctive conditions: foreign country AND CO impracticability finding. Provides flexibility for overseas operations.

Natural_Language: Treasury issues supplements to Treasury Department Circular 570, notifying all Federal agencies of new approved corporate surety companies and the termination of the authority of any specific corporate surety to qualify as a surety on Federal bonds. Upon receipt of notification of termination of a company's authority to qualify as a surety on Federal bonds, the contracting officer must review the outstanding contracts and take action necessary to protect the Government, including, where appropriate, securing new bonds with acceptable sureties in lieu of outstanding bonds with the named company.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_202_c_a: Treasury issues supplements to Circular 570 for new approvals and terminations; P_28_202_c_b: Upon termination notification CO must review outstanding contracts and take protective action
Validation_Notes: Reactive obligation triggered by Treasury termination notification. CO must both review AND act. 'Including where appropriate securing new bonds' is illustrative of protective action. Declarative first clause about Treasury supplements.

Natural_Language: Treasury Department Circular 570 may be obtained from the U.S. Department of the Treasury, Bureau of the Fiscal Service, Surety Bond Branch, 3201 Pennsy Drive, Building E, Landover, MD 20785 or at https://www.fiscal.treasury.gov/fsreports/ref/suretyBnd/c570.htm.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_202_d: Circular 570 available from Treasury Bureau of Fiscal Service at specified address and URL
Validation_Notes: Informational provision. No regulatory obligation. Provides access information for reference document.

Natural_Language: Individual sureties (parent aggregating 28.203-1 through 28.203-5).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_203: Individual surety requirements as specified in 28.203-1 through 28.203-5
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating five subsections on individual sureties.

Natural_Language: Acceptability of individual sureties (parent aggregating (a)-(g)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_203_1: Individual surety acceptability requirements as specified in (a) through (g)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating seven paragraphs on individual surety acceptability.

Natural_Language: An individual surety is acceptable for all types of bonds except position schedule bonds. Assets pledged by an individual surety must meet the eligibility requirements of Treasury's Bureau of the Fiscal Service. Per 31 U.S.C. 9310, individual sureties must pledge eligible obligations, which Treasury refers to as acceptable collateral or eligible collateral.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_203_1_a_1: Individual surety acceptable for all bond types except position schedule bonds; P_28_203_1_a_2: Pledged assets must meet Treasury Bureau of Fiscal Service eligibility; P_28_203_1_a_3: Per 31 USC 9310 must pledge eligible obligations
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Broad acceptability with one exception plus mandatory asset requirements. Position schedule bond exclusion is absolute. Asset eligibility governed by external Treasury and statutory requirements (31 USC 9310).

Natural_Language: Individual surety bond execution requirements (parent aggregating (1)-(4)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_203_1_b: Bond execution requirements as specified in (1) through (4)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating four bond execution sub-requirements.

Natural_Language: An individual surety must execute the bond (e.g., bid bond (SF 24), performance bond (SF 25), payment bond (SF 25A)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_203_1_b_1: Individual surety must execute the bond using applicable SF (24/25/25A)
Validation_Notes: Mandatory execution requirement. Forms are illustrative of bond types. Cross-references SF 24, SF 25, SF 25A.

Natural_Language: The net adjusted value of unencumbered assets is their market value minus the margin. The margin tables are available at www.treasurydirect.gov. The net adjusted value of unencumbered assets pledged by the individual surety must equal or exceed the penal amount (i.e., face value) of each bond.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_203_1_b_2_a: Net adjusted value = market value minus margin; P_28_203_1_b_2_b: Margin tables at treasurydirect.gov; P_28_203_1_b_2_c: Net adjusted value must >= penal amount of each bond
Validation_Notes: Valuation formula and minimum threshold. Mandatory: net adjusted value must meet or exceed penal amount. Margin tables are external Treasury reference.

Natural_Language: The individual surety must execute the SF 28, Affidavit of Individual Surety, and provide a security interest. One individual surety is adequate support for a bond, provided the net adjusted value of unencumbered assets pledged by that individual surety equals or exceeds the amount of the bond.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_203_1_b_3_a: Must execute SF 28 and provide security interest; P_28_203_1_b_3_b: One surety is adequate if net adjusted value >= bond amount
Validation_Notes: Two requirements. First: mandatory execution and security interest. Second: one-surety adequacy conditioned on value threshold. Cross-references SF 28.

Natural_Language: An offeror or contractor may submit up to three individual sureties for each bond, in which case the net adjusted value of the pledged unencumbered assets, when combined, must equal or exceed the penal amount of the bond. Each individual surety is jointly and severally liable to the extent of the penal amount of the bond.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_203_1_b_4_a: Up to three individual sureties per bond; P_28_203_1_b_4_b: Combined NAV must >= penal amount; P_28_203_1_b_4_c: Each surety jointly and severally liable to penal amount
Validation_Notes: Permissive multi-surety option with mandatory financial and liability requirements. Combined value threshold applies when multiple sureties used. Joint and several liability is mandatory characteristic.

Natural_Language: Using the information from the SF 28 submitted by the offeror or contractor, the contracting officer must notify the Treasury's collateral operations support team by email at BMT@fiscal.treasury.gov or by phone at 888-568-7343, of the individual surety, the assets to be pledged, and the amount necessary to cover the individual surety bond. Treasury will advise the contracting officer whether the assets are eligible to be pledged and of the valuation of the assets offered. If after 3 business days the contracting officer has not received a response from Treasury, the contracting officer may seek assistance from the Director, Bank Policy and Oversight, at 202-504-3502. The contracting officer must determine whether the individual surety bond is acceptable as to the amount necessary based on the asset eligibility and valuation assessment from Treasury. The contracting officer must notify both the offeror or contractor and the individual surety of this determination.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_203_1_c_1: CO must notify Treasury collateral team of surety/assets/amount; P_28_203_1_c_2: Treasury advises on asset eligibility and valuation; P_28_203_1_c_3: If no Treasury response in 3 business days CO may escalate; P_28_203_1_c_4: CO must determine acceptability based on Treasury assessment; P_28_203_1_c_5: CO must notify offeror/contractor and surety of determination
Formal_Logic_Statement: SF_28_Submitted -> (Notify_Treasury ^ Await_Assessment); (~Treasury_Response_3_Days -> (Escalate v ~Escalate)); Treasury_Assessment -> CO_Determine_Acceptability; CO_Determination -> Notify_All_Parties
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Complex multi-step procedural sequence. Mandatory notification to Treasury, mandatory determination based on assessment, mandatory notification of result. Escalation after 3 days is permissive. External process dependency on Treasury response.

Natural_Language: If the contracting officer determines the individual surety is acceptable, the contracting officer must request the Treasury's collateral operations support team set up the necessary individual surety pledged asset collateral account.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_203_1_d: If CO determines surety acceptable then must request Treasury set up collateral account
Validation_Notes: Mandatory follow-on action triggered by acceptability determination. External process dependency on Treasury account setup.

Natural_Language: If the contracting officer determines that no individual surety in support of a bid guarantee is acceptable, the offeror utilizing the individual surety must be rejected as nonresponsible, except as provided in 28.101-4. A finding of nonresponsibility based on unacceptability of an individual surety, need not be referred to the Small Business Administration for a Certificate of Competency. (See part 19 and 61 Comp. Gen. 456 (1982).)
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_203_1_e_1: If no acceptable individual surety for bid guarantee then reject offeror as nonresponsible except per 28.101-4; P_28_203_1_e_2: No SBA COC referral required for this nonresponsibility finding
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Two-part rule. First: mandatory rejection with cross-reference exception to 28.101-4 waiver provisions. Second: exemption from SBA COC process. Cross-references Part 19. Significant small business implication. GAO decision cited.

Natural_Language: If a contractor submits an unacceptable individual surety, or one that Treasury could not assess the asset eligibility and valuation within a reasonable time, then the contracting officer may permit the contractor to substitute an acceptable surety within a reasonable time.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_203_1_f: If unacceptable surety or Treasury cannot assess then CO may permit substitution
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Addition (Add): Rule 8; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Permissive remedial authority. Disjunctive trigger: either unacceptable surety OR Treasury assessment failure. CO discretion on whether to permit substitution. 'Reasonable time' is undefined.

Natural_Language: Evidence of possible criminal or fraudulent activities by an individual surety must be referred to the appropriate agency official in accordance with agency procedures.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_203_1_g: Evidence of criminal/fraudulent activity by individual surety must be referred per agency procedures
Validation_Notes: Mandatory referral obligation. Disjunctive trigger: criminal OR fraudulent activity evidence. Agency procedures govern the specific referral process.

Natural_Language: An individual surety may request the Government to accept a substitute asset for that currently pledged by submitting a written request, including a revised SF 28, to the responsible contracting officer. Following the requirements set forth in 28.203-1, the contracting officer may agree to the substitution of assets upon determining that the substitute assets to be pledged are adequate to protect the outstanding bond or guarantee obligations.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_203_2_a: Individual surety may request asset substitution via written request with revised SF 28; P_28_203_2_b: CO may agree upon determining substitute assets adequate
Validation_Notes: Permissive substitution process. Surety initiates with written request plus revised SF 28. CO discretion to agree conditional on adequacy determination. Must follow 28.203-1 procedures. Cross-references SF 28 and 28.203-1.

Natural_Language: Release of security interest (parent aggregating (a)-(c)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_203_3: Release of security interest requirements as specified in (a) through (c)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating three paragraphs on security interest release.

Natural_Language: After consultation with legal counsel, the contracting officer must release the security interest on the individual surety's assets using the Optional Form 91, Release of Personal Property from Escrow, or a similar release as soon as possible consistent with the conditions in subparagraphs (a)(1) and (2) of this section. A surety's assets pledged in support of a payment bond may be released to a subcontractor or supplier upon Government receipt of a Federal district court judgment, or a sworn statement by the subcontractor or supplier that the claim is correct along with a notarized authorization of the release by the surety stating that it approves of such release.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_203_3_a_1: CO must release security interest using OF 91 after legal counsel consultation; P_28_203_3_a_2: Release as soon as possible per conditions in (1)-(3); P_28_203_3_a_3: Payment bond assets may be released to sub upon court judgment or sworn statement with surety authorization
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Complex release provision. Mandatory release with legal counsel consultation and OF 91 form. Timing governed by sub-paragraph conditions. Payment bond asset release to subs is permissive with disjunctive evidentiary bases. Cross-references OF 91.

Natural_Language: Contracts subject to the Bonds statute. The security interest must be maintained for the later of- (parent with (i)-(iii)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_203_3_a_1: For Bonds statute contracts security maintained for the latest of three periods
Validation_Notes: Conditional retention period. 'Later of' means whichever period ends last governs. Three disjunctive time periods with the longest controlling.

Natural_Language: 1 year following final payment.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_203_3_a_1_i: Security maintained for 1 year following final payment
Validation_Notes: First retention period option. Atomic time requirement.

Natural_Language: Until completion of any warranty period (applicable only to performance bonds).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_203_3_a_1_ii: Security maintained until warranty completion (performance bonds only)
Validation_Notes: Second retention period option. Restricted to performance bonds only. If no warranty no applicability.

Natural_Language: Pending resolution of all claims filed against the payment bond during the 1 year period following final payment.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_203_3_a_1_iii: Security maintained pending resolution of all claims filed during 1-year post-final-payment period
Validation_Notes: Third retention period option. Open-ended: security held until ALL claims resolved. Applies to payment bond claims filed within the 1-year window.

Natural_Language: Contracts subject to alternative payment protection. The security interest must be maintained for the full contract performance period plus 1 year.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_203_3_a_2: For alternative payment protection contracts security maintained for full performance period plus 1 year
Validation_Notes: Fixed retention formula: performance period + 1 year. Simpler than Bonds statute retention which has three variable endpoints.

Natural_Language: Other contracts not subject to the Bonds statute. The security interest must be maintained for 90 days following final payment or until completion of any warranty period (applicable only to performance bonds), whichever is later.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_203_3_a_3: For other non-Bonds statute contracts security maintained for later of 90 days after final payment or warranty completion (performance bonds)
Validation_Notes: Retention for contracts outside Bonds statute. 'Later of' two periods. 90-day baseline with warranty extension for performance bonds only. Shorter baseline than Bonds statute 1-year requirement.

Natural_Language: Upon written request by the individual surety, the contracting officer may release the security interest on the individual surety's assets in support of a bid guarantee based upon evidence that the offer supported by the individual surety will not result in contract award.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_203_3_b: Upon surety written request CO may release bid guarantee security if evidence offer will not result in award
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Permissive early release of bid guarantee security. Conjunctive conditions: written request AND evidence of no award. CO retains discretion.

Natural_Language: Upon written request by the individual surety, the contracting officer may release a portion of the security interest on the individual surety's assets based upon substantial performance of the contractor's obligations under its performance bond. Release of the security interest in support of a payment bond must comply with the subparagraphs (a)(1) through (3) of this section. In making this determination, the contracting officer will give consideration as to whether the unreleased portion of the security is sufficient to cover the remaining contract obligations, including payments to subcontractors and other potential liabilities. The individual surety must, as a condition of the partial release, furnish an affidavit agreeing that the release of such assets does not relieve the individual surety of its obligations under the bond(s).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_203_3_c_1: CO may partially release performance bond security upon substantial performance; P_28_203_3_c_2: Payment bond release must comply with (a)(1)-(3); P_28_203_3_c_3: CO must consider sufficiency of unreleased portion; P_28_203_3_c_4: Surety must furnish affidavit as condition
Formal_Logic_Statement: (Surety_Request ^ Substantial_Performance) -> (Partial_Release v ~Partial_Release); Payment_Bond_Release -> Comply_With_a_1_thru_3; Partial_Release -> (Consider_Sufficiency ^ Surety_Affidavit_Required)
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Multi-condition partial release. Permissive for performance bond security. Payment bond release governed by (a)(1)-(3) retention periods. Two mandatory conditions on any partial release: sufficiency consideration and surety affidavit.

Natural_Language: Solicitation provision and contract clause (parent aggregating (a)-(b)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_203_4: Individual surety clause requirements as specified in (a) and (b)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating two clause insertion requirements for individual sureties.

Natural_Language: Insert the provision at 52.228-17, Individual Surety - Pledge of Assets (Bid Guarantee), in solicitations that require the submission of a bid guarantee.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_203_4_a: Insert 52.228-17 in solicitations requiring bid guarantee submission
Validation_Notes: Mandatory provision insertion conditional on bid guarantee requirement. Cross-references 52.228-17.

Natural_Language: Insert the clause at 52.228-11, Individual Surety - Pledge of Assets, in solicitations and contracts that require the submission of performance or payment bonds.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_203_4_b: Insert 52.228-11 in solicitations/contracts requiring performance or payment bonds
Validation_Notes: Mandatory clause insertion. Disjunctive trigger: either performance or payment bond requirement. Cross-references 52.228-11.

Natural_Language: Exclusion of individual sureties (parent aggregating (a)-(e)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_203_5: Individual surety exclusion requirements as specified in (a) through (e)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating five paragraphs on individual surety exclusion authority and procedures.

Natural_Language: An individual may be excluded from acting as a surety on bonds submitted by offerors on procurement by the executive branch of the Federal Government, by the acquiring agency's head or designee utilizing the procedures in part 9. The exclusion must be for the purpose of protecting the Government.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_203_5_a_1: Individual may be excluded from acting as surety by agency head/designee using Part 9 procedures; P_28_203_5_a_2: Exclusion must be for purpose of protecting Government
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Permissive exclusion authority with three conjunctive conditions: appropriate authority AND proper procedures AND protective purpose. Cross-references Part 9 debarment/suspension procedures.

Natural_Language: Causes for exclusion (parent listing (1)-(5)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_203_5_b: Causes for individual surety exclusion as listed in (1) through (5)
Validation_Notes: Parent listing five disjunctive causes. Any single cause is sufficient for exclusion.

Natural_Language: Failure to fulfill the obligations under any bond.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_203_5_b_1: Failure to fulfill obligations under any bond
Validation_Notes: First exclusion cause. Atomic. Performance failure on any bond, not limited to specific bond.

Natural_Language: Failure to disclose all bond obligations.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_203_5_b_2: Failure to disclose all bond obligations
Validation_Notes: Second exclusion cause. Atomic. Transparency/disclosure failure.

Natural_Language: Misrepresentation of the value of available assets or outstanding liabilities.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_203_5_b_3: Misrepresentation of asset value or outstanding liabilities
Validation_Notes: Third exclusion cause. Disjunctive: misrepresentation of either assets or liabilities.

Natural_Language: Any false or misleading statement, signature or representation on a bond or affidavit of individual suretyship.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_203_5_b_4: False/misleading statement or signature or representation on bond or affidavit
Formal_Logic_Statement: (False_Statement v Misleading_Statement v False_Signature v False_Representation) ^ (On_Bond v On_Affidavit)
Validation_Notes: Fourth exclusion cause. Broad coverage: any type of false/misleading element on either document type.

Natural_Language: Any other cause affecting responsibility as a surety of such serious and compelling nature as may be determined to warrant exclusion.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_203_5_b_5: Any other cause of serious and compelling nature warranting exclusion
Validation_Notes: Fifth exclusion cause. Catch-all provision. Discretionary standard: 'serious and compelling nature' requires judgment.

Natural_Language: An individual surety excluded pursuant to this section must be entered as an exclusion in the System for Award Management (SAM) (see part 9).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_203_5_c: Excluded individual surety must be entered in SAM
Validation_Notes: Mandatory administrative action following exclusion. Cross-references Part 9 and SAM system.

Natural_Language: Contracting officers must not accept the bonds of individual sureties whose names appear in an active exclusion record in SAM unless the acquiring agency's head or a designee state in writing the compelling reasons justifying acceptance.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_203_5_d: CO must not accept excluded surety bonds unless agency head provides written compelling reasons
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Prohibition with narrow exception. Default is rejection of excluded surety bonds. Override requires agency head written justification with compelling reasons. High threshold for exception.

Natural_Language: An exclusion of an individual surety under this section will also preclude such party from acting as a contractor in accordance with part 9.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_203_5_e: Surety exclusion also precludes acting as contractor per Part 9
Validation_Notes: Cross-preclusion: surety exclusion extends to contractor capacity. Mandatory consequence. Cross-references Part 9.

Natural_Language: Alternatives in lieu of corporate or individual sureties (parent aggregating (a)-(c)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_204: Alternative security requirements as specified in (a) through (c)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating three paragraphs on alternatives to sureties.

Natural_Language: Any person required to furnish a bond to the Government may furnish any of the types of security listed in 28.204-1 through 28.204-3 instead of a corporate or individual surety for the bond. When any of those types of security are deposited, a statement must be incorporated in the bond form pledging the security in lieu of execution of the bond form by corporate or individual sureties. The contractor must execute the bond forms as the principal. Agencies must establish safeguards to protect against loss of the security and must return the security or its equivalent to the contractor when the bond obligation has ceased.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_204_a_1: Any person may furnish 28.204-1 through 28.204-3 security instead of surety; P_28_204_a_2: Must incorporate pledging statement in bond form; P_28_204_a_3: Contractor must execute bond forms as principal; P_28_204_a_4: Agencies must establish safeguards against loss; P_28_204_a_5: Must return security when bond obligation ceased
Formal_Logic_Statement: Bond_Required -> (Use_Alternative_Security v ~Use_Alternative_Security); Alternative_Security -> (Pledging_Statement ^ Execute_As_Principal ^ Agency_Safeguards ^ Return_When_Ceased)
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Permissive alternative with four mandatory implementation requirements. Any bond obligor may use alternatives. When used: pledging statement, principal execution, agency safeguards, and return obligation all apply conjunctively. Cross-references 28.204-1 through 28.204-3.

Natural_Language: Upon written request by any contractor securing a performance or payment bond by any of the types of security listed in 28.204-1 through 28.204-3, the contracting officer may release a portion of the security only when the conditions allowing the partial release of security in 28.203-3(c) are met. The contractor must, as a condition of the partial release, furnish an affidavit agreeing that the release of such security does not relieve the contractor of its obligations under the bond(s).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_204_b_1: CO may partially release alternative security when 28.203-3(c) conditions met; P_28_204_b_2: Contractor must furnish affidavit as condition of release
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Permissive partial release conditioned on 28.203-3(c) requirements. Mandatory affidavit for any partial release. Parallel to individual surety release provisions. Cross-references 28.203-3(c).

Natural_Language: The contractor may satisfy a requirement for bond security by furnishing a combination of the types of security listed in 28.204-1 through 28.204-3 or a combination of bonds supported by these types of security and additional surety bonds under 28.202 or 28.203. During the period for which a bond supported by security is required, the contractor may substitute one type of security listed in 28.204-1 through 28.204-3 for another, or may substitute, in whole or combination, additional surety bonds under 28.202 or 28.203.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_204_c_1: Contractor may use combination of 28.204-1 through 28.204-3 security types; P_28_204_c_2: May combine alternative security with surety bonds under 28.202 or 28.203; P_28_204_c_3: May substitute security types during bond period; P_28_204_c_4: May substitute surety bonds for alternative security
Formal_Logic_Statement: Contractor -> ((Combination_204_Types v Combination_204_Plus_Surety) v ~Use_Combination); Bond_Period -> ((Substitute_204_Types v Substitute_Surety_For_204) v ~Substitute)
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Addition (Add): Rule 8; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Broad permissive flexibility. Contractor may mix and match security types and may substitute during the bond period. All 'may' language indicates full discretion. Cross-references 28.204-1 through 28.204-3, 28.202, 28.203.

Natural_Language: Any person required to furnish a bond to the Government has the option, instead of furnishing a surety or sureties on the bond, of depositing certain United States bonds or notes in an amount equal at their par value to the penal sum of the bond (the Act of February 24, 1919 (31 U.S.C. 9303) and Treasury Department Circular No. 154 (31 CFR part 225)). In addition, a duly executed power of attorney and agreement authorizing the collection or sale of such United States bonds or notes in the event of default of the principal on the bond must accompany the deposited bonds or notes. The contracting officer may- (parent with (a)-(b)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_204_1_1: Any person may deposit US bonds/notes at par value equal to penal sum in lieu of surety; P_28_204_1_2: Power of attorney and agreement authorizing collection/sale on default must accompany deposit
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Permissive alternative with mandatory documentation. Statutory authority from 31 USC 9303. Par value must equal penal sum. POA and default collection/sale agreement are mandatory accompaniments. External statutory and regulatory dependencies.

Natural_Language: Turn securities over to the finance or other authorized agency official.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_204_1_a: CO may turn deposited securities over to finance or authorized agency official
Validation_Notes: First CO option for handling deposited securities. Atomic disposition option.

Natural_Language: Deposit them with the Treasurer of the United States, a Federal Reserve Bank (or branch with requisite facilities), or other depository designated for that purpose by the Secretary of the Treasury, under procedures prescribed by the agency concerned and Treasury Department Circular No. 154 (exception: The contracting officer must deposit all bonds and notes received in the District of Columbia with the Treasurer of the United States).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_204_1_b_1: CO may deposit with Treasurer of US or Federal Reserve Bank or designated depository; P_28_204_1_b_2: DC exception: must deposit with Treasurer of US
Formal_Logic_Statement: (Deposit_With_Treasurer v Deposit_With_FRB v Deposit_With_Designated); DC_Receipt -> Deposit_With_Treasurer_Only
Validation_Notes: Three disjunctive deposit options with DC mandatory exception. Securities received in DC must go to Treasurer of US. External procedural dependency on Treasury Circular 154.

Natural_Language: Any person required to furnish a bond has an option to furnish a certified or cashier's check, bank draft, Post Office money order, or currency, in an amount equal to the penal sum of the bond, instead of furnishing surety or sureties on the bonds. Those furnishing checks, drafts, or money orders must draw them to the order of the appropriate Federal agency.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_204_2_a: Person may furnish certified check or cashier check or bank draft or money order or currency equal to penal sum in lieu of surety; P_28_204_2_b: Checks/drafts/money orders must be drawn to order of appropriate agency
Formal_Logic_Statement: Bond_Required -> (Certified_Check v Cashier_Check v Bank_Draft v Money_Order v Currency); (Check v Draft v Money_Order) -> Drawn_To_Agency_Order
Validation_Notes: Five disjunctive payment instrument options. Mandatory payee requirement for non-currency instruments. Amount must equal penal sum. Straightforward alternative to sureties.

Natural_Language: Irrevocable letter of credit (parent aggregating (a)-(h)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_204_3: ILC requirements as specified in (a) through (h)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating eight paragraphs on ILC requirements. Most detailed alternative security provision.

Natural_Language: Any person required to furnish a bond has the option to furnish a bond secured by an irrevocable letter of credit (ILC) in an amount equal to the penal sum required to be secured (see 28.204). A separate ILC is required for each bond.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_204_3_a_1: Person may furnish bond secured by ILC equal to penal sum; P_28_204_3_a_2: Separate ILC required for each bond
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Permissive ILC option with mandatory one-to-one bond requirement. Amount must equal penal sum. Cross-references 28.204.

Natural_Language: The ILC must be irrevocable, require presentation of no document other than a written demand and the ILC (and letter of confirmation, if any), expire only as provided in paragraph (f) of this subsection, and be issued/confirmed by an acceptable federally insured financial institution as provided in paragraph (g) of this subsection.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_204_3_b_1: ILC must be irrevocable; P_28_204_3_b_2: Must require only written demand and ILC for presentation; P_28_204_3_b_3: Must expire only per (f); P_28_204_3_b_4: Must be issued/confirmed by acceptable federally insured institution per (g)
Validation_Notes: Four conjunctive mandatory ILC characteristics. All must be present. Cross-references (f) for expiration and (g) for institution requirements.

Natural_Language: To draw on the ILC, the contracting officer must use the sight draft set forth in the clause at 52.228-14, and present it with the ILC (including letter of confirmation, if any) to the issuing financial institution or the confirming financial institution (if any).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_204_3_c: To draw on ILC CO must use sight draft from 52.228-14 and present with ILC to issuing/confirming institution
Validation_Notes: Mandatory procedure for ILC draw. Two conjunctive requirements: specific sight draft form AND presentation to appropriate institution. Cross-references 52.228-14.

Natural_Language: If the contractor does not furnish an acceptable replacement ILC, or other acceptable substitute, at least 30 days before an ILC's scheduled expiration, the contracting officer must immediately draw on the ILC.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_204_3_d: If no acceptable replacement/substitute ILC 30 days before expiration then CO must immediately draw
Validation_Notes: Mandatory protective action triggered by contractor failure to provide timely replacement. 'Must immediately' leaves no discretion. 30-day threshold is hard deadline.

Natural_Language: If, after the period of performance of a contract where ILCs are used to support payment bonds, there are outstanding claims against the payment bond, the contracting officer must draw on the ILC prior to the expiration date of the ILC to cover these claims.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_204_3_e: If post-performance outstanding payment bond claims exist then CO must draw on ILC before expiration
Validation_Notes: Mandatory draw to protect against claims. Three conjunctive conditions trigger the obligation. Timing requirement: before ILC expiration.

Natural_Language: The period for which financial security is required must be as follows: (parent with (1)-(2)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_204_3_f: ILC required financial security periods as specified in (1) and (2)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating bid guarantee and performance/payment bond security periods.

Natural_Language: If used as a bid guarantee, the ILC should expire no earlier than 60 days after the close of the bid acceptance period.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_204_3_f_1: Bid guarantee ILC should expire no earlier than 60 days after bid acceptance close
Validation_Notes: Advisory timing ('should' not 'must'). Minimum 60-day post-acceptance expiration. Provides buffer for award processing.

Natural_Language: If used as an alternative to corporate or individual sureties as security for a performance or payment bond, the offeror/contractor may submit an ILC with an initial expiration date estimated to cover the entire period for which financial security is required or an ILC with an initial expiration date that is a minimum period of one year from the date of issuance. The ILC must provide that, unless the issuer provides the beneficiary written notice of non-renewal at least 60 days in advance of the current expiration date, the ILC is automatically extended without amendment for one year from the expiration date, or any future expiration date, until the period of required coverage is completed and the contracting officer provides the financial institution with a written statement waiving the right to payment. The period of required coverage must be: (parent for Bonds statute and other).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_204_3_f_2_a: Offeror may submit ILC covering entire period or with 1-year minimum initial expiration; P_28_204_3_f_2_b: ILC must auto-extend unless 60-day non-renewal notice; P_28_204_3_f_2_c: Required coverage period per sub-paragraphs
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Complex ILC structure provision. Disjunctive initial term options. Mandatory auto-extension mechanism with 60-day non-renewal notice. Required coverage periods in sub-paragraphs. Multiple mandatory elements.

Natural_Language: For contracts subject to the Bonds statute, the later of- (parent with (A)-(C)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_204_3_f_2_i: Bonds statute contracts: coverage for latest of three periods
Validation_Notes: Parallel to 28.203-3(a)(1). Three disjunctive periods with longest controlling. Bonds statute applicability trigger.

Natural_Language: One year following the expected date of final payment.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_204_3_f_2_i_A: Coverage for 1 year following expected final payment date
Validation_Notes: First coverage period option. Note 'expected date' vs 28.203-3(a)(1)(i) which says 'final payment' -- ILC coverage starts from expected date.

Natural_Language: For performance bonds only, until completion of any warranty period.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_204_3_f_2_i_B: Performance bonds only: coverage until warranty completion
Validation_Notes: Second coverage period option. Restricted to performance bonds. Parallel to 28.203-3(a)(1)(ii).

Natural_Language: For payment bonds only, until resolution of all claims filed against the payment bond during the one-year period following final payment.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_204_3_f_2_i_C: Payment bonds only: coverage until all claims resolved from 1-year post-final-payment period
Validation_Notes: Third coverage period option. Restricted to payment bonds. Open-ended until all claims resolved. Parallel to 28.203-3(a)(1)(iii).

Natural_Language: For contracts not subject to the Bonds statute, the later of- (parent with (A)-(B)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_204_3_f_2_ii: Non-Bonds statute contracts: coverage for latest of two periods
Validation_Notes: Parallel to 28.203-3(a)(3). Two disjunctive periods with longest controlling. Shorter requirements than Bonds statute contracts.

Natural_Language: 90 days following final payment.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_204_3_f_2_ii_A: Coverage for 90 days following final payment
Validation_Notes: First non-Bonds statute coverage period. Shorter than the 1-year Bonds statute equivalent.

Natural_Language: For performance bonds only, until completion of any warranty period.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_204_3_f_2_ii_B: Performance bonds only: coverage until warranty completion
Validation_Notes: Second non-Bonds statute coverage period. Performance bonds only. Identical concept to Bonds statute equivalent at (i)(B).

Natural_Language: Only federally insured financial institutions rated investment grade must issue or confirm the ILC. Unless the financial institution issuing the ILC had letter of credit business of at least $25 million in the past year, ILCs over $5 million must be confirmed by another acceptable financial institution that had letter of credit business of at least $25 million in the past year. (Parent with (1)-(3)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_204_3_g_1: Only federally insured investment-grade institutions may issue/confirm ILC; P_28_204_3_g_2: ILCs >$5M require confirmation by institution with >=$25M LC business unless issuer also meets threshold
Validation_Notes: Two-tier institutional requirement. Base: federal insurance and investment grade. Enhanced: confirmation requirement for large ILCs from smaller institutions. $25M LC business threshold creates tiered access. Cross-references (1)-(3) for verification procedures.

Natural_Language: The offeror/contractor is required by paragraph (d) of the clause at 52.228-14, Irrevocable Letter of Credit, to provide the contracting officer a credit rating from a recognized commercial rating service that indicates the financial institution has the required rating(s) as of the date of issuance of the ILC.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_204_3_g_1: Offeror must provide credit rating per 52.228-14(d) showing institution meets rating requirement at ILC issuance
Validation_Notes: Mandatory documentation requirement. Rating must be current as of ILC issuance date. Cross-references 52.228-14(d).

Natural_Language: To support the credit rating of the financial institution(s) issuing or confirming the ILC, the contracting officer must verify the following information: (parent with (i)-(ii)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_204_3_g_2: CO must verify federal insurance and credit rating for ILC institutions
Validation_Notes: Mandatory CO verification obligation. Two sub-elements must be verified conjunctively.

Natural_Language: Federal insurance: Each financial institution is federally insured. Verification of federal insurance is available through the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) institution directory at the website http://www2.fdic.gov/idasp/index.asp.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_204_3_g_2_i: CO must verify each institution is federally insured via FDIC directory
Validation_Notes: First verification item. FDIC directory is the prescribed verification source. External dependency on FDIC.

Natural_Language: Current credit rating. The current credit rating for each financial institution is investment grade and that the credit rating is from a Nationally Recognized Statistical Rating Organization (NRSRO). NRSROs can be located at the website http://www.sec.gov/answers/nrsro.htm maintained by the SEC.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_204_3_g_2_ii: CO must verify current investment-grade rating from NRSRO
Validation_Notes: Second verification item. Investment grade from NRSRO required. SEC website for NRSRO identification. External dependency on SEC/NRSROs.

Natural_Language: The rating services listed in the website http://www.sec.gov/answers/nrsro.htm use different rating scales (e.g., AAA, AA, A, BBB, BB, B, CCC, CC, C, and D; or Aaa, Aa, A, Baa, Ba, B, Caa, Ca, and C) to provide evaluations of institutional credit risk; however, all such systems specify the range of investment grade ratings (e.g., BBB-AAA or Baa-Aaa in the examples in this section) and permit evaluation of the relative risk associated with a specific institution. If the contracting officer learns that a financial institution's rating has dropped below investment grade level, the contracting officer must give the contractor 30 days to substitute an acceptable ILC or must draw on the ILC using the sight draft in paragraph (g) of the clause at 52.228-14.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_204_3_g_3_a: Rating agencies use different scales but all specify investment grade range; P_28_204_3_g_3_b: If institution rating drops below investment grade CO must give 30 days to substitute or draw on ILC
Validation_Notes: Informational context on rating scales plus mandatory reactive action. Rating downgrade triggers disjunctive CO obligation: either allow 30-day substitution OR draw immediately. Not permissive; CO must take one action. Cross-references 52.228-14(g).

Natural_Language: A copy of the Uniform Customs and Practice for Documentary Credits, 2007 Edition, International Chamber of Commerce Publication No. 600, is available from: ICC Books USA, 1212 Avenue of the Americas, 21st Floor, New York, NY 10036.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_204_3_h: UCP 600 (ICC Publication No. 600) available from ICC Books USA
Validation_Notes: Informational provision. No regulatory obligation. Reference document availability for ILC practices.

Natural_Language: Insert the clause at 52.228-14, Irrevocable Letter of Credit, in solicitations and contracts for services, supplies, or construction, when a bid guarantee, or performance bonds, or performance and payment bonds are required.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_204_4: Insert 52.228-14 when bid guarantee or performance bonds or performance and payment bonds required for any contract type
Validation_Notes: Mandatory clause insertion with disjunctive trigger. Any bond/guarantee requirement triggers the ILC clause. Applies to services, supplies, and construction. Cross-references 52.228-14.

Natural_Language: Policy (parent aggregating (a)-(c)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_301: Insurance policy requirements as specified in (a) through (c)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating three paragraphs on insurance policy.

Natural_Language: Contractors must carry insurance under the following conditions in accordance with law and agency regulations (see CAS 416 at 48 CFR 9904.416 for additional requirements): (parent with (1)-(3)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_301_a: Contractor insurance requirements per law, agency regulations, and CAS 416
Validation_Notes: Parent mandate. External dependencies on CAS 416 (48 CFR 9904.416) and agency regulations. Three sub-conditions aggregated conjunctively.

Natural_Language: The Government requires the contractor to provide insurance. Reasons for requiring insurance include, but are not limited to, the following: (parent with (i)-(ii) as exceptions).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_301_a_1: Government requires contractor insurance except in listed circumstances
Justification_Rules: Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: General insurance requirement with two exceptions. The sub-paragraphs (i) and (ii) are situations where insurance is NOT required, forming disjunctive exceptions.

Natural_Language: It is not in the Government's interest to require the contractor to carry insurance and the Government agrees to indemnify the contractor against certain liabilities.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_301_a_1_i: Exception when Government agrees to indemnify contractor and insurance not in Government interest
Validation_Notes: First exception. Both conditions must hold conjunctively: not in Government interest AND Government agrees to indemnify.

Natural_Language: The contract, together with the Government's property policy, provides adequate protection to the Government's interest and a clause prescribed pursuant to the requirements of 28.303 is included in the contract.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_301_a_1_ii: Exception when contract plus Government property policy provides adequate protection and 28.303 clause included
Validation_Notes: Second exception. Two conjunctive conditions: adequate protection AND required clause inclusion. Cross-references 28.303.

Natural_Language: The Government reserves the right to disapprove the purchase of any insurance coverage not in the Government's interest.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_301_a_2: Government reserves right to disapprove insurance not in its interest
Validation_Notes: Declarative reservation of rights. Atomic proposition. Unilateral Government authority.

Natural_Language: The allowability of the cost of insurance is determined in accordance with 31.205-19.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_301_a_3: Insurance cost allowability determined per 31.205-19
Validation_Notes: Cross-reference to cost principle. External dependency on FAR 31.205-19 for insurance cost allowability determinations.

Natural_Language: Contractors carrying insurance required by law, regulation, or contract must provide insurance of the types and in the minimum amounts required. These minimum amounts may be reduced when a contract is to be performed in a foreign country. Agencies may prescribe procedures for negotiating insurance requirements that provide broader coverage at lower rates on a fleet or comprehensive basis.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_301_b_1: Contractors must provide required insurance types in minimum amounts; P_28_301_b_2: Minimum amounts may be reduced for foreign country performance; P_28_301_b_3: Agencies may prescribe procedures for fleet/comprehensive coverage negotiation
Formal_Logic_Statement: Insurance_Required -> (Required_Types ^ Minimum_Amounts); Foreign_Country -> (Reduce_Minimums v ~Reduce_Minimums); Agency -> (Prescribe_Fleet_Procedures v ~Prescribe_Fleet_Procedures)
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Three-part provision: mandatory compliance, permissive foreign country reduction, and permissive agency fleet procedures.

Natural_Language: Contracts for nonpersonal health care service contracts can specify that contractors providing medical services are required to have medical liability insurance.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_301_c: Nonpersonal health care service contracts may require medical liability insurance
Validation_Notes: Permissive authority to require medical liability insurance for nonpersonal health care services. 'Can specify' indicates discretion.

Natural_Language: All types of insurance required by the contract must provide for notification to the Government when the policy or policies are substantially changed, canceled, or allowed to expire. When the coverage is provided by self-insurance, the contractor must not change or decrease the coverage without the administrative contracting officer's prior approval (see 28.308).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_302_a: Required insurance must notify Government of substantial change/cancellation/expiration; P_28_302_b: Self-insurance changes require ACO prior approval
Validation_Notes: Two mandatory requirements. First: notification obligation for all insurance types. Second: prior approval requirement specifically for self-insurance changes. Cross-references 28.308.

Natural_Language: The Government may require a contractor to obtain insurance against loss of or damage to Government property in the contractor's possession or control, by inserting in the contract the clause at 52.228-8, Liability and Insurance - Leased Motor Vehicles. The circumstances under which such insurance may be required include, but are not limited to, situations in which a nongovernmental source is required because (a) the Government's self-insurance against the perils to which the property will be exposed is inappropriate, and (b) the circumstances are such that the risk should not be retained by the Government.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_303_a: Government may require insurance against loss/damage to Government property; P_28_303_b: Required when Government self-insurance inappropriate and risk should not be retained
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Permissive authority with illustrative conditions. Two conjunctive conditions describe when requirement is appropriate but are not exhaustive. Cross-references 52.228-8.

Natural_Language: Agency heads may establish risk-pooling arrangements. These arrangements are designed to use the services of the insurance industry for administration of the program and are intended to result in lower insurance costs for Government contract work.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_304: Agency heads may establish risk-pooling arrangements using insurance industry services for lower costs
Validation_Notes: Permissive authority at agency head level. Policy rationale is lower costs. No mandatory requirements.

Natural_Language: Overseas workers' compensation and war-hazard insurance (parent aggregating (a)-(e)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_305: Overseas workers comp and war-hazard insurance as specified in (a) through (e)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating five paragraphs on overseas insurance requirements.

Natural_Language: As used in this section, public-work contract means any contract for the construction, alteration, or repair, including painting or decorating, of public buildings or public works, and which requires or involves the employment of mechanics or laborers.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_305_a: Public-work contract defined as construction/alteration/repair of public buildings/works requiring mechanics or laborers
Formal_Logic_Statement: (Construction v Alteration v Repair) ^ Public_Buildings_Or_Works ^ Requires_Mechanics_Or_Laborers -> Public_Work_Contract
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Addition (Add): Rule 8; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7
Validation_Notes: Definitional proposition. Disjunctive work types (construction OR alteration OR repair) combined conjunctively with public buildings/works scope and labor requirement.

Natural_Language: The Defense Base Act (42 U.S.C. 1651, et seq.) extends the Longshore and Harbor Workers' Compensation Act (33 U.S.C. 901) to various classes of employees working outside the United States, including those engaged in- (parent with (1)-(2)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_305_b: DBA extends LHWCA to employees working outside US in specified categories
Validation_Notes: Statutory framework provision. DBA is the extending statute; LHWCA is the underlying coverage. Two disjunctive categories of covered employment. External statutory dependencies on 42 USC 1651 and 33 USC 901.

Natural_Language: Public-work contracts with the Government.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_305_b_1: DBA covers employees on public-work contracts with Government
Validation_Notes: First DBA coverage category. Public-work contract as defined in (a).

Natural_Language: Contracts approved or financed under the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961, other than- (parent with (i)-(ii) as exclusions).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_305_b_2: DBA covers Foreign Assistance Act contracts except listed exclusions
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Second DBA coverage category with disjunctive exclusions. Foreign Assistance Act contracts covered unless one of two exclusions applies.

Natural_Language: Contracts approved or financed by the Development Loan Fund (unless the party to whom the loan is made specifically applies, with the approval of the Secretary of Labor, for DBA coverage).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_305_b_2_i: Development Loan Fund contracts excluded unless borrower applies for DBA coverage with Secretary of Labor approval
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: First exclusion with re-inclusion mechanism. Default is excluded. Re-included only if borrower applies AND Secretary of Labor approves. Conjunctive re-inclusion conditions.

Natural_Language: Contracts exclusively for materials or supplies.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_305_b_2_ii: Contracts exclusively for materials or supplies excluded from DBA
Validation_Notes: Second exclusion. 'Exclusively' is key qualifier; mixed contracts would not qualify for exclusion.

Natural_Language: When the Defense Base Act applies, the contractor is required to provide the workers' compensation and war-hazard insurance benefits prescribed by the Act. When the Defense Base Act applies, the War Hazards Compensation Act (42 U.S.C. 1701, et seq.) automatically extends protection on a reciprocal basis.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_305_c_1: When DBA applies contractor must provide prescribed workers comp and war-hazard benefits; P_28_305_c_2: When DBA applies WHCA automatically extends reciprocal protection
Validation_Notes: DBA applicability triggers two conjunctive consequences: mandatory contractor benefits AND automatic WHCA extension. External statutory dependency on 42 USC 1701.

Natural_Language: The Secretary of Labor may waive the applicability of the Defense Base Act to any contract, subcontract, work location, or classification of employees.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_305_d: Secretary of Labor may waive DBA applicability to contracts/subcontracts/locations/employee classifications
Validation_Notes: Permissive waiver authority at Secretary of Labor level. Broad scope: can waive for specific contracts, locations, or employee classes.

Natural_Language: If the Defense Base Act is waived, the War Hazards Compensation Act is automatically waived. If the contractor provides the workers' compensation coverage, the contractor may have a liability not covered by the Defense Base Act insurance. The contractor may have statutory liability under the laws of the country in which the work is being performed; under the Longshore and Harbor Workers' Compensation Act, as extended by the Defense Base Act, or under State workers' compensation laws. In addition, the contractor or the Government may have liability for civil damages under the laws of a country in which the work is being performed.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_305_e_1: DBA waiver automatically waives WHCA; P_28_305_e_2: Contractor may have uncovered liability under various laws; P_28_305_e_3: Contractor must provide coverage and assume liability
Validation_Notes: Automatic WHCA waiver follows DBA waiver. Multiple potential liability sources identified. Contractor bears residual liability risk. Complex interaction of domestic and foreign law.

Natural_Language: Insurance under fixed-price contracts (parent aggregating (a)-(b)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_306: Fixed-price contract insurance as specified in (a) and (b)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating general policy and Government installation requirements.

Natural_Language: Except when the Government's interest would not be served, or when the clause at 52.228-5 is used as specified in 28.310(a), fixed-price contractors and subcontractors are ordinarily responsible for obtaining insurance to cover losses to which they may be exposed in performing the contract. The Government is not ordinarily concerned with the contractor's insurance coverage except for certain conditions: (parent with (1)-(4)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_306_a: Fixed-price contractors ordinarily responsible for own insurance; Government generally unconcerned except in four special circumstances
Formal_Logic_Statement: Fixed_Price_Contract -> Contractor_Responsible_For_Insurance; Government_Concerned_When -> (P_28_306_a_1 v P_28_306_a_2 v P_28_306_a_3 v P_28_306_a_4)
Validation_Notes: Default rule for fixed-price with disjunctive exceptions. Government normally not involved. Four circumstances trigger Government interest.

Natural_Language: The contractor is, or has a separate operation, engaged principally in Government work.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_306_a_1: Contractor principally engaged in Government work
Validation_Notes: First Government-concern circumstance. Atomic condition.

Natural_Language: Government property is involved.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_306_a_2: Government property involved in contract performance
Validation_Notes: Second Government-concern circumstance. Atomic condition.

Natural_Language: The work is performed on a Government installation.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_306_a_3: Work performed on Government installation
Validation_Notes: Third Government-concern circumstance. Atomic condition. Key trigger for 28.310 clause requirement.

Natural_Language: The Government elects to assume certain risks.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_306_a_4: Government elects to assume certain risks
Validation_Notes: Fourth Government-concern circumstance. Atomic condition. Discretionary Government election.

Natural_Language: Work on a Government installation (parent with (1)-(2)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_306_b: Insurance requirements for work on Government installation as specified in (1) and (2)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating two scenarios based on 52.228-5 applicability.

Natural_Language: When the clause at 52.228-5 is required by 28.310, the minimum insurance requirements must be those set forth in 28.307-2.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_306_b_1: When 52.228-5 required per 28.310 then minimum insurance per 28.307-2
Validation_Notes: Conditional linkage: 52.228-5 requirement triggers 28.307-2 minimums. Cross-references 28.310 and 28.307-2.

Natural_Language: When the clause at 52.228-5 is not required by 28.310, but is included in the contract, the insurance types and minimum amounts included in the clause may be omitted or the minimum amounts may be lowered.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_306_b_2: When 52.228-5 not required but included then types may be omitted or minimums lowered
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Permissive relaxation when clause is voluntary. CO may omit insurance types or lower minimums. Flexibility for non-mandatory inclusion.

Natural_Language: Insurance under cost-reimbursement contracts.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_307: Insurance requirements for cost-reimbursement contracts
Validation_Notes: Section header establishing cost-reimbursement insurance context. Parent for 28.307-1 and 28.307-2.

Natural_Language: Group insurance plans (parent aggregating (a)-(b)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_307_1: Group insurance plan requirements as specified in (a) and (b)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating two group insurance requirements.

Natural_Language: When the Government requires a contractor to buy insurance under a group insurance plan, the contracting officer must obtain the prior approval of the contracting officer before buying insurance under a group plan. Any change in benefits provided under an approved plan requires similar prior approval.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_307_1_a: Prior approval required before buying insurance under group plan; benefit changes also require approval
Validation_Notes: Two mandatory approval requirements. Both initial purchase and subsequent benefit changes require prior CO approval. Gate-keeping mechanism for Government cost control.

Natural_Language: Any plan for which the Government incurs a portion of the premium cost must provide for the Government to share in any refund or credits arising out of the plan's experience, in a proportion equal to the Government's share of the premium cost.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_307_1_b: When Government shares premium cost it must share proportionally in refunds/credits
Validation_Notes: Mandatory proportional sharing. Government's refund share equals its premium share. Prevents contractor windfall from Government-funded premiums.

Natural_Language: Liability (parent aggregating (a)-(e)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_307_2: Liability insurance requirements as specified in (a) through (e)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating five categories of liability insurance.

Natural_Language: Workers' compensation and employer's liability. Contractors are required to comply with applicable Federal and State workers' compensation and occupational disease statutes. If occupational diseases are not compensable under those statutes, they must be covered under the employer's liability section of the insurance policy, except when contract operations are so commingled with a contractor's commercial operations that it would not be practical to require this coverage. Employer's liability coverage of at least $100,000 must be required, except in States with exclusive or monopolistic funds that do not permit workers' compensation to be written by private carriers.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_307_2_a_1: Contractor must comply with Federal/State workers comp statutes; P_28_307_2_a_2: Occupational diseases not covered by statute must be covered under employer liability except when commingled; P_28_307_2_a_3: Employer liability minimum $100K except in exclusive/monopolistic fund States
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Three-layer requirement. Base: statutory compliance. Middle: occupational disease gap-fill except commingled operations. Top: $100K minimum except exclusive fund States. Multiple exceptions create complex conditional structure.

Natural_Language: General liability (parent with (1)-(2)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_307_2_b: General liability insurance as specified in (1) and (2)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating bodily injury and property damage general liability.

Natural_Language: Bodily injury liability insurance coverage written on the comprehensive form of policy of at least $500,000 per occurrence.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_307_2_b_1: Bodily injury liability at least $500K per occurrence on comprehensive form
Validation_Notes: Mandatory minimum: $500K per occurrence. Must be comprehensive form policy. Two conjunctive requirements.

Natural_Language: Property damage liability insurance must be required only in special circumstances as determined by the agency.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_307_2_b_2: Property damage liability required only in special circumstances per agency determination
Validation_Notes: Permissive/conditional requirement. Not standard; only when agency determines special circumstances exist. Discretionary.

Natural_Language: Automobile liability. The contracting officer must require automobile liability insurance written on the comprehensive form of policy. The policy must provide for bodily injury and property damage liability covering the operation of all automobiles used in connection with performing the contract. Policies must provide coverage of at least $200,000 per person and $500,000 per occurrence for bodily injury and $20,000 per occurrence for property damage.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_307_2_c_1: CO must require comprehensive auto liability insurance; P_28_307_2_c_2: Must cover all automobiles used in contract performance; P_28_307_2_c_3: Minimums: $200K/$500K bodily injury and $20K property damage
Validation_Notes: Five conjunctive mandatory requirements for auto liability. Comprehensive form, full auto coverage, and three specific dollar minimums.

Natural_Language: Aircraft public and passenger liability. When contract operations involve use of aircraft, the contracting officer must require aircraft public and passenger liability insurance. Coverage must be at least $200,000 per person and $500,000 per occurrence for bodily injury, other than passenger liability, and $200,000 per occurrence for property damage. Coverage for passenger liability bodily injury must be at least $200,000 multiplied by the number of seats or passengers, whichever is greater.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_307_2_d_1: When aircraft used CO must require aircraft public and passenger liability; P_28_307_2_d_2: $200K/$500K bodily injury and $200K property damage; P_28_307_2_d_3: Passenger liability at least $200K per seat/passenger whichever greater
Validation_Notes: Conditional on aircraft use. Five conjunctive requirements including passenger liability formula based on seats or passengers (whichever greater).

Natural_Language: Vessel liability. When contract operations involve use of vessels, the contracting officer must require, as determined by the agency, parsing collision liability and protection and indemnity liability insurance.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_307_2_e: When vessels used CO must require collision and P&I liability insurance as determined by agency
Validation_Notes: Conditional on vessel use. Two conjunctive insurance types required. Amounts left to agency determination unlike auto and aircraft which have specified minimums.

Natural_Language: Self-insurance (parent aggregating (a)-(f)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_308: Self-insurance requirements as specified in (a) through (f)
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating six paragraphs on self-insurance approval and requirements.
