Natural_Language: When it is anticipated that 50 percent or more of the self-insurance costs will be allocable to Government contract work and the self-insurance costs at the time the program was submitted for approval or the costs incurred/estimated to be incurred under the program total $200,000 or more per year, the contractor must submit the self-insurance program to the administrative contracting officer and the contract auditor for approval. The submission must include, as a minimum, the following: (parent with (1)-(10)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_308_a: When >=50% allocable to Government AND >=$200K/year then submit self-insurance program to ACO and auditor
Validation_Notes: Conditional submission requirement. Two conjunctive thresholds: >=50% Government allocation AND >=$200K annual cost. Triggers mandatory submission to both ACO and auditor with 10 minimum documentation items.

Natural_Language: A complete description of the program, including any reinsurance agreements, and the types of risks, exposures, and liabilities it is designed to cover.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_308_a_1: Complete description of self-insurance program including reinsurance and coverage scope
Validation_Notes: First documentation item. Atomic minimum submission element.

Natural_Language: A copy of the corporate insurance manual and organizational chart reflecting the responsibilities for the management of the program.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_308_a_2: Corporate insurance manual and org chart for program management
Validation_Notes: Second documentation item. Atomic minimum submission element.

Validation_Notes: Tenth documentation item. Financial management procedures including conditional catastrophic fund element.

Natural_Language: Programs of self-insurance covering a contractor's insurable risks, including the deductible portion of purchased insurance, may be approved when examination of a program indicates the probable cost to the Government will be less than the cost of providing the same coverage by purchase of insurance. Self-insurance must not be approved when the Government may be required to contribute to a self-insurance fund or reserve for the purpose of meeting the contractor's obligations under workers' compensation laws, unless the fund or reserve is limited to- (parent with (1)-(2)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_308_b_1: Self-insurance approved when probable Government cost less than purchased insurance; P_28_308_b_2: Not approved for workers comp fund obligations unless limited per (1)-(2)
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Permissive approval with cost-effectiveness test plus mandatory prohibition on workers comp self-insurance except under two limited circumstances. Dual conditional structure.

Natural_Language: The self-insurance program is approved by a State authority having jurisdiction over workers' compensation and the contractor maintains an approved self-insurance program that covers the employer's liability and any workers' compensation not covered by the State fund.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_308_b_1: State authority approves AND contractor maintains self-insurance covering employer liability and uncovered workers comp
Validation_Notes: First workers comp exception. Two conjunctive conditions: State approval AND maintained coverage for gaps.

Natural_Language: The combined cost of the self-insurance program and purchased insurance that will be charged the Government will not be greater than the cost of all purchased insurance.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_308_b_2: Combined self-insurance and purchased insurance cost to Government must not exceed all-purchased cost
Validation_Notes: Second workers comp exception. Cost-effectiveness test: combined approach must not exceed full purchased insurance cost.

Natural_Language: The contractor must submit any major change in the program for the Government's approval before the change is implemented. Any changes in the program that could increase the cost of coverage to the Government require a new determination of the probable cost to the Government of the changed program. Approval may be withdrawn when the Government determines the program does not comply with this subpart or 31.205-19 or when the conditions under which the program was initially approved have changed to the extent that continued approval is not in the interest of the Government. (parent with (1)-(2) as withdrawal causes).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_308_c_1: Contractor must submit major changes for prior approval; P_28_308_c_2: Cost-increasing changes need new cost determination; P_28_308_c_3: Approval may be withdrawn per (1)-(2)
Formal_Logic_Statement: Major_Change -> Prior_Gov_Approval; Cost_Increase_Change -> New_Cost_Determination; (P_28_308_c_1_cond v P_28_308_c_2_cond) -> (Withdraw_Approval v ~Withdraw_Approval)
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Three-part provision: mandatory change submission, mandatory re-determination for cost increases, and permissive approval withdrawal under two causes. Cross-references 31.205-19.

Natural_Language: The program does not comply with the requirements of this subpart or 31.205-19.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_308_c_1: Program does not comply with Subpart 28.3 or 31.205-19
Validation_Notes: First withdrawal cause. Disjunctive: noncompliance with either the subpart or the cost principle.

Natural_Language: The conditions under which the program was initially approved have changed to the extent that continued approval is not in the interest of the Government.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_308_c_2: Changed conditions make continued approval not in Government interest
Validation_Notes: Second withdrawal cause. Conjunctive: conditions changed AND no longer in Government interest.

Natural_Language: To qualify for approval of a self-insurance program, the contractor must demonstrate ability to sustain the potential losses involved. In making the determination whether self-insurance is practical, the contracting officer must consider the following: (parent with (1)-(5)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_308_d: Contractor must demonstrate loss-sustaining ability; CO considers five factors
Validation_Notes: Mandatory qualification requirement with five evaluation factors. Contractor bears burden of demonstration; CO evaluates per listed factors.

Natural_Language: The soundness of the contractor's financial condition, including available lines of credit.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_308_d_1: CO considers soundness of financial condition including credit lines
Validation_Notes: First evaluation factor. Financial capacity assessment.

Natural_Language: The geographic dispersion of assets, so that the corporation is not subject to the risk of a single loss depleting its total assets.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_308_d_2: CO considers geographic dispersion of assets for risk diversification
Validation_Notes: Second evaluation factor. Concentration risk assessment.

Natural_Language: The history of previous losses, including their frequency and severity.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_308_d_3: CO considers loss history frequency and severity
Validation_Notes: Third evaluation factor. Historical loss pattern analysis.

Natural_Language: The type and magnitude of risk, e.g., minor potential for loss versus catastrophic loss.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_308_d_4: CO considers type and magnitude of risk
Validation_Notes: Fourth evaluation factor. Risk profile assessment.

Natural_Language: The contractor's compliance with Federal and State laws and regulations.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_308_d_5: CO considers compliance with Federal and State laws and regulations
Validation_Notes: Fifth evaluation factor. Regulatory compliance assessment.

Natural_Language: Agencies must not approve a self-insurance program to cover risks for which the Government requires the contractor to carry insurance under terms that provide for, or require, the Government to indemnify the contractor or to pay for any portion of the premium costs. Agencies may, however, approve a self-insurance program to cover risks for which the Government has elected to assume the risks.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_308_e_1: Must not approve self-insurance for risks requiring Government indemnification or premium payment; P_28_308_e_2: May approve for Government-assumed risks
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Addition (Add): Rule 8; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Prohibition with permissive exception. Cannot self-insure when Government bears indemnification or premium cost. Can self-insure when Government has elected to assume risks. Prevents double benefit to contractor.

Natural_Language: Self-insurance programs to cover risks for the purpose of correcting defects in the contractor's own products or work must not be approved. The Government assumes no obligation for losses that are the contractor's own responsibility under the terms of the contract.
Atomic_Propositions: P_28_308_f: Self-insurance for correcting own product/work defects must not be approved
Validation_Notes: Absolute prohibition. No self-insurance for contractor's own defect correction. Government explicitly disclaims liability. No exceptions.
